ECCLESIASTICUS 4:4  Cast thou not away the praying of a man set in tribulation, and turn not away thy face from a needy man. [The praying of the troubled not cast thou away, and turn thou not away thy face from the needy.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:5  Turn not away thine eyes from a poor man for ire [or wrath], and give not occasion, [or cause], to men ask-ing to curse thee (from) behind.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:6  For the prayer of him that curseth thee in the bitterness of soul, shall be heard; forsooth he that made him, shall hear him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:7  Make thee easy to speak to the congregation of poor men, and make meek thy soul to a priest, that is, do thou due reverence to an eld man, and make meek thine head to a great man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:8  Bow down without sorrow thine ear to a poor man [or to the poor], and yield thy debt, and answer thou peaceably in mildness (or with meekness).
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:9  Deliver thou him that suffereth wrong from the hand of a proud man, and bear thou not heavily in thy soul (when deeming).
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:10  In deeming be thou merciful as a father to fatherless children, and be thou for an husband to the mother of them; and thou shalt be as an obedient son of the Highest, and he shall have mercy on thee more than a mother hath mercy on her child.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:11  Wisdom inspireth [or inbreathed] life to his (or to its) sons, and receiveth men seeking him (or it), and shall go before (them) in the way of rightfulness [or rightwiseness];
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:12  and he that loveth that wisdom, loveth life, and they that wake to it, shall embrace the peaceableness, [or the gladness], either sweetness, thereof.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:13  They that hold it, shall inherit life; and whither it shall enter, God shall bless.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:14  They that serve it, shall be obeying to the Holy (One); and God loveth them, that love it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:15  He that heareth it, deemeth folks; and he that beholdeth it, shall dwell trustily.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:16  If a man believeth to it [or give faith to it], he shall dwell, and inherit it; and the creatures of them shall be in confirming, that is, the works of them shall be confirmed in good.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:17  For in temptation it goeth with him, and among the first it chooseth him. It shall bring in on him dread, and fear, and proving, and it shall torment him in the tribulation of his doctrine [or his teaching], till it tempt him in his thoughts, and (it) believe to (or in) his soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:18  And it shall make him steadfast, and shall bring (the) right way to him, and it shall make him glad; and shall make naked his privates to him (or shall make open his secrets to him), and shall treasure on him cunning (or knowing), and understanding of rightfulness [or rightwiseness].
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:19  Forsooth if he erreth, God[or it] shall forsake him, and shall betake him into the hands of his enemy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:20  Son, keep thou [or wait (on)](the) time, and eschew thou [or shun away] from evil. Be thou not ashamed (even) for thy life to say (the) truth;
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:21  for why there is shame that bringeth sin, and there is shame that bringeth glory and grace.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:22  Take thou not a face against thy face, that is, against thy soul, neither a leasing (or a lie) against thy soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:23  Shame thou not thy neighbour in his fall[ing], neither withhold thou a word in the time of health.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:24  Hide not thy wisdom in the fairness thereof; for why wisdom is known in (the) tongue, and wit, and cunning (or knowing), and teaching in the word of a wise man; and stead-fastness is in the works of rightfulness [or rightwiseness].
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:25  Against-say thou not (or Say thou not against) the word of truth in any manner; and be thou ashamed of the leasing (or lies) of thy mis-learning.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:26  Be thou not ashamed to acknowl-edge thy sins; and make thee not subject to each man for sin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:27  Do not thou stand against [or withstand] the face of the mighty, neither enforce (or endeavor) thou against the stroke of the flood (or the river).
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:28  For rightfulness fight thou for the health of thy soul, and till to the death strive thou for rightfulness; and God shall overcome thine enemies for thee. [For rightwiseness fight for thy soul, and unto death strive for rightwiseness; and God shall outfight, or overcome, for thee thine enemies.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:29  Do not thou be swift in (or with) thy tongue, and unprofitable and slack, [or sloth(ful)], in (or with) thy works.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:30  Do not thou be as a lion in thine house, turning upside down thy menials, and oppressing them that be subject/s to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 4:31  Thine hand be not ready to take, and closed (al)together to give.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:1  Do not thou take heed to wicked possessions, and say thou not, Sufficient life is to me [or There is to me sufficient life], that is, long is to coming to me, therefore I must get many things; for it shall nothing profit in the time of vengeance, and of failing [or oppressing], either death.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:2  Pursue thou not the covetousness of thine heart in thy strength, [Not follow thou in thy strength the coveting of thine heart,]
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:3  and say thou not, As I might, either, who shall make me subject for my deeds? For why God avenging shall avenge.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:4  Say thou not, I have sinned, and what sorrowful thing befell to me? For the Highest is a patient yielder.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:5  Of the forgiveness of sins, do not thou be without dread, neither heap thou, [or lay thou], sin upon sin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:6  And say thou not, The merciful doing of God is great [or The mercy of God is great]; he shall have mercy on the multitude of my sins. For why mercy and ire nigheth soon from him, and his ire beholdeth on sinners.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:7  Tarry thou not to be converted to the Lord, and delay thou not [or put thou it off] from day into day. For why his ire shall come suddenly, and he shall lose (or destroy) thee in the time of vengeance.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:8  Do not thou be anguished in unjust [or unright] riches; for those [or they] shall not profit in the day of failing, either of death, and of vengeance.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:9  Winnow thee not into each wind, and go thou not into each way; for so a sinner is proved in (or with a) double tongue.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:10  Be thou steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in truth and cunning (or the knowing) of thy wit; and the word of peace and of rightfulness [or of rightwiseness] pursue thee perfectly.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:11  Be thou mild (or meek) to hear the word of God, (so) that thou understand, and with wisdom bring thou forth a true answer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:12  If thou hast understanding, answer thy neighbor; else thine hand be on thy mouth, lest thou be taken (or caught) in a word unwisely taught, and be ashamed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:13  Honour and glory is in the word of a wise man; but the tongue of an unprudent man is his destroying.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:14  Be thou not called a privy evil speaker in thy life, and be thou not taken in (or with) thy tongue, and be ashamed. Shame and penance is on a thief, and worst shame, either cursing, is on a man of (or with a) double tongue. Forsooth hatred and enmity and despising is to a privy backbiter.
ECCLESIASTICUS 5:15  Justify thou a little man and a great man [or the little and the great] in like manner.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:1  Do not thou for a friend (or instead of a friend) be made (an) enemy to thy neighbour; for why an evil man shall inherit upbraiding and despising, and each sinner envious and double-tongued.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:2  Enhance thee not in the thought of thy soul, as a bull doeth; lest thy virtue [or strength] be hurtled down by folly,
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:3  and it eat thy leaves, and lose (or destroy) thy fruits, and thou be left as a dry tree in (the) desert [or (the) wilderness].
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:4  Forsooth a wicked, [or shrewd, (or depraved)] soul shall lose [or destroy] him that hath it, and it giveth him into the joy of the enemy, and it shall lead forth into the part of wicked men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:5  A sweet word multiplieth friends, and assuageth enemies; and a tongue well gracious shall be plenteous [or abound] in a good man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:6  Many peaceable men be to thee, and (or but) one (out) of a thousand be a counsellor to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:7  If thou hast a friend, have him in temptation, that is, prove thou him in thine adversity, and betake not lightly [or not lightly open, or trust], thyself to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:8  For there is a friend by (or for) his (own) time, and he shall not dwell [or abide] in the day of tribulation.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:9  And there is a friend which is turned to enmity; and there is a friend, that shall show openly hatred, and chiding [or strife], and despisings.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:10  Forsooth there is a friend, (a) fellow of (the) table, and (he) dwell-eth not in the day of need.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:11  If a friend dwelleth steadfast, he shall be as a man even with thee, and he shall do trustily in (or with) thy menial [or homely] things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:12  If he meeketh himself before thee, and hideth him(self) from thy face, thou shalt have good friendship of one accord [or of one will].
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:13  Be thou parted from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:14  A faithful friend is a strong defending [or strong protection]; for-sooth he that findeth him, findeth treasure.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:15  No comparison is to a faithful friend; weighing of gold and of silver is not worthy against the goodness of his faithfulness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:16  A faithful friend is(the) medicine of life, and of undeadliness (or of immortality); and they that dread the Lord, shall find him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:17  He that dreadeth the Lord, shall have evenly good friendship; for why his friend shall be at the likeness of him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:18  Son, from thy youth take thou doctrine, and till to [thine] hoar hairs thou shalt find wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:19  As he that eareth (or ploweth), and that soweth, nigh thou to it, and abide thou (for) the good fruits there-of. For thou shalt travail a little in the work thereof, and thou shalt eat soon of the generations thereof [or the gettings of it].
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:20  Wisdom is over-sharp or is full-sharp to untaught men, and an heart-less man shall not dwell therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:21  As the virtue (or the strength) of a stone, proving shall be in them; and they shall not tarry to cast away it [or to throw it afar].
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:22  Forsooth the wisdom of teaching is by the name thereof, and it is not open to many men; but it dwelleth with them, of whom it is known, till to the sight of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:23  Son, hear thou, and take the counsel of understanding, and cast thou not away my counsel.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:24  Set in thy foot into the stocks thereof, and thy neck into the bies, (or the bands), [or the collars] thereof.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:25  Make subject thy shoulder, and bear it, and be thou not annoyed (or harmed) in the bonds thereof.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:26  In all thy will go to it, and in all thy virtue keep the ways thereof [or of it].
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:27  Inquire thou (of or about) it [or Ensearch it], and it shall be made open to thee; and thou made holding wisdom forsake not it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:28  For in the last things thou shalt find rest therein, and it shall turn [or shall be turned] to thee into delight-ing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:29  And the stocks thereof shall be to thee in defence [or protection] of strength, and the foundaments of virtue, and the bie(s), (or the bands), [or the collars] thereof, in(to) a stole of glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:30  For why the fairness of life is in wisdom, and the bonds thereof be heal(th)ful, [or wholesome] binding.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:31  Thou shalt wear it as a stole of glory, and thou shalt set [or shalt put] on thee a crown of thanking.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:32  Son, if thou takest heed to me, thou shalt learn wisdom; and if thou givest thy will, thou shalt be wise.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:33  If thou bowest down thine ear, thou shalt take (or receive) teaching; and if thou lovest for to hear, thou shalt be wise.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:34  Stand thou in the multitude of prudent priests, and be thou joined of (or in) heart to the wisdom of them;
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:35  (so) that thou mayest hear each telling of God, and the proverbs of praising flee or fly not away from thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:36  And if thou seest a wise man, wake thou to him, and thy foot [often] tread on the grees (or the steps) of his doors.
ECCLESIASTICUS 6:37  Have thou thought in (or on) the commandments of God, and be thou most busy in his behests; and he shall give to thee [an] heart, and covetous-ness of wisdom shall be given to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:1  Do not thou do evils, and those shall not take [or catch] thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:2  Depart thou from wickedness [or Go away from the wicked], and evils shall fail from thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:3  Sow thou not evils in the furrows of unrightfulness [or unrightwiseness], and thou shalt not reap those in sevenfold.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:4  Do not thou seek of (or from) a man (the) leading [or the dignity of a leader], neither of a king the chair of honour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:5  Justify thou not thee (or thyself) before God, for he is the knower of the heart; and do not thou desire to be seen wise with the king.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:6  Do not thou seek to be made a judge, no but thou mayest break wickednesses by (thy) virtue; lest thou dread the face of a mighty man, and set slander (or a cause of stumbling) in thy swiftness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:7  Do not thou sin in (or against) the multitude of a city, neither send thee, (or thyself), (down) into the people;
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:8  neither bind thou [to] double sins, for thou shalt not be guiltless in one.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:9  Do not thou be a coward in thy soul, to pray; and despise thou not to do alms-[deeds].
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:10  Say thou not, God shall behold in the multitude of my gifts; and when I shall offer to God alder-Highest [or to the highest God], he shall take my gifts.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:11  Scorn thou not a man in the bitterness of (his) soul; for why God is the beholder, that maketh meek, and enhanceth (or exalteth).
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:12  Do not thou love a leasing (or a lie) against thy brother; neither do thou in like manner against a friend.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:13  Do not thou desire to lie any leasing (or any lie); for why the continuance thereof [or the busyness forsooth of them] is not good.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:14  Do not thou be a jangler [or full of words] in the multitude of priests; and rehearse thou not a word in thy prayer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:15  Hate thou not travailous works, and earth-tilthing, [or churlish doing] made of (or from) the Highest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:16  Areckon thou not thee in the multitude of unlearned men. Have thou mind on ire [or wrath], for it shall not tarry.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:17  Make thou meek greatly thy spirit, for why the vengeance of the flesh of an unpious man is fire, and worm(s).
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:18  Do not thou trespass against thy friend delaying money; neither despise thou a full dearworth(y) brother for gold.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:19  Do not thou depart [or go away] from a wise woman, and good, whom thou hast gotten in the dread of the Lord; for why the grace of her shame-fastness is above gold.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:20  Hurt thou not a servant working in truth, neither an hired man giving his life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:21  A witty, (or a witting, or knowing) servant be dearworthy to thee as thy (own) soul; defraud thou not him of freedom, neither forsake thou him (when) needy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:22  Beasts be to thee? take thou heed to those [or them]; and if those [or they] be profitable, dwell those still at [or with] thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:23  Sons be to thee? teach thou them, and bow thou them under chastising from their childhood.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:24  Daughters be to thee? keep thou the body of them, and show thou not (a) glad face to them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:25  Give thy daughter to marriage, and thou doest a great work; and give thou her to a wise man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:26  If a woman is to thee after thy soul, cast her not away; and (or but) betake thou not thee in all thine heart to an hateful woman.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:27  Honour thy father; and forget thou not the wailings of thy mother.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:28  Have thou mind that thou haddest not been, no but by them, and yield thou to them as they did to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:29  In all thy soul dread thou God, and hallow thou his priests.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:30  In all thy virtue (or strength) love thou him that made thee; and forsake thou not his ministers [or servants].
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:31  Honour thou God of (or with) all thy soul; and honour thou priests, and cleanse thee with (thine) arms, that is, by offerings gotten with thy travail. Give thou to them the part of the first fruits, and of purging, as also it is commanded to thee; and of thy negligence purge thou thee with few men. Thou shalt offer to the Lord the gift of thine arms, and the sacrifice of hallowing, the beginnings, that is, the first fruits and dimes (or tithes), of holy men [or holy things].
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:32  And (ad)dress (or direct)[or put forth] thine hand to a poor man, (so) that thy mercy and (thy) blessing be performed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:33  Grace is given [or Grace of gift] in the sight of each that liveth; and forbid thou not grace to a dead man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:34  Fail thou not in (or to do) comfort to them that weep; and go thou with them that mourn.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:35  Be thou not slow to visit a sick man [or the sick]; for by these things thou shalt be made steadfast in love.
ECCLESIASTICUS 7:36  In all thy works have thou mind on [or have in mind] thy last things; and thou shalt not do sin without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:1  Chide [or Strive] thou not with a mighty man, lest thou fall into his hands.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:2  Strive thou not with a rich man, lest peradventure he make (a) play again-ward to (or towards) thee [or he set strife to thee]. For why gold and silver hath lost (or destroyed) many men; and it stretcheth forth till to the heart[s] of kings, and turneth (them).
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:3  Chide thou not with a man, a jangler, [or Strive thou not with a tonguey man], and lay thou not trees into his fire.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:4  Commune thou not with an untaught man, lest he speak evil of thy kindred.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:5  Despise thou not a man turning away himself from sin, neither upbraid thou him [nor put thou reproof to him]; have thou mind, that all we be in corruption.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:6  Despise thou not a man in his eld (age); for why (some) of us men wax eld [or old].
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:7  Do not thou make joy of (or over) thine enemy (being) dead, witting that all we die (or knowing that we all die), and will (or desire) not (to) come into joy of (or with) our enemies.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:8  Despise thou not the telling of wise priests, and be thou conversant [or (al)together dwell] in the proverbs of them; for of (or from) them thou shalt learn wisdom, and teaching of understanding, and to serve without (com)plaint to great men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:9  The telling of elder men pass not (by) thee; for they have learned of (or from) their fathers. For of (or from) them thou shalt learn understanding; and in the time of need thou shalt give [an] answer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:10  Kindle thou not the coals of sinners, and reprove them; and be thou not burnt with the flame of [the] fire of their sins.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:11  Stand thou not against the face of a man full of despising [or of the strifeful]; lest he sit as an espyer to thy mouth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:12  Do not thou lend to a man stronger than thou [or than thyself]; that (or but) if thou hast lent, have thou it as lost.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:13  Promise thou not above [or over] thy power or virtue; that (or but) if thou hast promised, bethink thou as yielding, for thou art holden to do thy might, (that is, thou art held to pay it back).
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:14  Deem thou not against a judge; for he deemeth after that, that is just.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:15  Go thou not in the way with an hardy man, lest peradventure he aggregate (or bring together all) his evils in (or on) thee; for he goeth after his (own) will (or desire), and thou shalt perish together with (him through) his folly.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:16  Make thou not chiding [or jangling] with a wrathful man, and go thou not into (a) desert with an hardy man; for why blood, that is, shedding out of innocent blood, is as nought before him, and where none help is, (or where there is no help), he shall hurtle thee down.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:17  Have thou not counsel with fools; for they may not (or be not able to) love, no but those things that please them(selves).
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:18  Make thou not a counsel before a stranger; for thou knowest not, what he shall bring forth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 8:19  Make not thine heart known to each man [or To all men thine heart open thou not], but only to a very (or a true) friend, and proved; lest peradventure he bring to thee false grace, that is, feigned friendship, and despise thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:1  Love thou not jealously the woman of thy bosom [or Be thou not jealous to the woman of thy bosom]; lest she show on thee the malice of evil doctrine.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:2  Give thou not to a woman the power of (or over) thy soul; lest she enter in thy virtue, and thou be shamed [or confounded].
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:3  Behold thou not a woman of many wills (or desires), that coveteth now this man, now that man; lest peradventure thou fall into the snares of her.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:4  Be thou not customable with a danceress, neither hire thou her; lest peradventure thou perish in the speedy work of her.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:5  Behold thou not a virgin [or a maiden]; lest peradventure thou be caused to stumble in (or by) the fairness of her.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:6  Give thou not thy soul to whores in anything; lest thou lose thee, and thy soul, and thine heritage, (or lest thou destroy thyself, and thy soul, and thy inheritance).
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:7  Do not thou behold about in the lanes of the city; neither err thou (or wander) in the large streets thereof. [Do thou not behold about in the ways of the city; nor err thou about in the streets of it.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:8  Turn away thy face from a woman well-arrayed; and behold thou not about the fairness of another or of another man’s wife. Many men have perished for the fairness of a woman; and thereby covetousness [or lust] burneth on high as fire or burneth out as fire. Each woman which is an whore, either customable to fornication, shall be defouled as a fen, or a turd, in the way. Many men wondering on the fairness of an alien woman were made reprovable, for why the speech of her burneth on high as fire.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:9  Sit thou not in any manner with an alien woman, neither rest thou with her on a bed [or nor lie thou with her upon the arm]; and jangle [or strive] thou not with her in wine, lest peradventure thine heart bow [or she bow down thine heart] into her, and thou fall [or slide] into perdition by thy blood.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:10  Forsake thou not an eld [or old] friend; for a new friend shall not be like him. New wine is(like) a new friend; (after) it shall wax eld [or old], and (then) thou shalt drink it with sweetness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:11  Covet thou not the glory and riches of a sinner; for thou knowest not, what destroying of him shall come. [Love thou not the glory and riches of the sinner; forsooth thou knowest not, what be to come (of) the turning upside-down of him.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:12  The wrong of unjust [or unright-wise] men please not thee, and know thou that a wicked man [or the unpious] shall not please till to hells, [or unto hell], (or the grave).
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:13  Be thou far from a man that hath power to slay, that is, from a cruel tyrant, and thou shalt not have suspicion of the dread of death; and if thou nighest to him, do not thou do any trespass [or anything do amiss], lest peradventure he take away thy life. Know thou the communing of death; for thou shalt enter into the midst of snares, and thou shalt go on the armours, [or arms], (or weapons) of them that sorrow.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:14  By thy virtue, keep thee (away) from thy neighbour that may speak against thee to a tyrant; and treat thou with wise men and prudent men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 9:15  Just [or Rightwise] men be guests, or meat-frères, (or meal companions) to thee; and thy glorying be in the dread of God.

ECCLESIASTICUS 9:18  A man, a jangler, [or a tonguey man], is dreadful [or fearful] in his city; and a foolhardy man in his word shall be hateful.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:1  A wise judge shall deem his people; and the princehood of a witty, (or a witting, or a knowing) man shall be steadfast [or be stable].
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:2  After the judge of the people, so and his ministers [or the servants of him]; and what manner man is the governor of the city, such be also men dwelling therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:3  An unwise king shall lose (or destroy) his people; and (or but) cities shall be inhabited by the wit of prudent men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:4  The power of (the) earth is in the hand of God, and all the wickedness of heathen men [or the Gentiles] is abominable; and he shall raise (up) a profitable governor at a time [or in (due) time] on it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:5  The power of man is in the hand of God; and he shall set his honour on the face of a wise man in the law [or the scribe].
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:6  Have thou not mind on all the wrong of the neighbour; and do thou nothing in the works of wrong-(doing).
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:7  Pride is hateful before God and men; and all the wickedness of (the) heathen men [or (the) Gentiles]is abominable.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:8  A realm is translated, either taken away, [or borne over], from a folk into folk for unrightfulnesses, and wrongs, and despisings, and diverse guiles, [or for unrightwisenesses, and wrongs, and strives, and diverse treacheries].
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:9  Nothing is curseder than an avarice man. What (or Why) art thou proud, thou earth and ashes? Nothing is worse, than for to love money, [or Nothing is more wicked, than to love money]; for why this man hath, yea, his soul set to (or for) sale, for in his life he hath cast away his innerest things, [or this forsooth hath his soul sellable, or able to be sold, for in his life he threw away his (most) inward things].
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:10  Each power is short life (or short-lived); long sickness [or infirmity] grieveth the leech (or the physician). A leech (or The physician) cutteth away [or cutteth off] short sickness; so and a king is today [or today is], and tomorrow he shall die.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:11  Forsooth when a man shall die, he shall inherit serpents, and beasts, and worms.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:12  The beginning of [the] pride of man was to be apostate [or to go backward] from God; for his heart went away from him that made him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:13  For why pride is the beginning of all sin [or For the beginning of all sin is pride]; he that holdeth it, shall be filled with cursings, and it shall destroy him into the end. Therefore the Lord hath shamed the covents, or convents, (or the gatherings) of evil men, and hath destroyed them unto the end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:14  God destroyed the seats (or the thrones) of proud dukes; and made mild men to sit for them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:15  God made dry the roots of proud folks; and planted meek men of those folks.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:16  The Lord destroyed the lands of folks [or Gentiles]; and lost those [or destroyed them] unto the foundament (or unto the foundation of the earth).
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:17  He made dry the roots of them, and lost (or destroyed) them; and made the mind of them (or their memory) to cease from the earth. God lost the mind of proud men; and left the mind of meek men in wit, (or God destroyed the memory of the proud; but left the memory of the humble).
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:18  Pride was not made to (or for) men; neither wrathfulness to (or for) the nation of women, that is, to all men born of women.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:19  This seed of men that dreadeth God, shall be honoured; but this seed shall be dishonoured, that over-pass-eth (or that passeth over) the commandments of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:20  In the midst of brethren the governor of them is in honour; and they that dread God, shall be in his eyes, that is, shall be honourable, and please him.

ECCLESIASTICUS 10:24  The judge is great, and he is mighty in honour; and (or but) he is not greater than that man that dread-eth God. [Great is a judge, and the mighty is in worship; and (or but) he is not more than he that dreadeth God.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 10:25  Free children serve a witty, (or a witting, or a knowing) servant; and a prudent man and learned shall not grutch (or grumble), when he is blamed, and an uncunning, (or an unknowing, or an ignorant) man shall not be honored.

ECCLESIASTICUS 11:1  The wisdom of a man made meek shall enhance his head; and shall make him to sit in the midst of great men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:2  Praise thou not a man in (or for) his fairness; neither despise thou a man in (or for) his sight.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:3  A bee is little among birds; and his fruit hath the beginning of sweet-ness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:4  Have thou never glory in cloth-ing, and be thou not enhanced (or exalted) in the day of thine honour; for why the works of the Highest alone be wonderful, and his works be glorious, and hid, and unseen.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:5  Many tyrants have set in (or upon a) throne; and a man of whom was no supposing bare the diadem (or crown).

ECCLESIASTICUS 11:7  Before that thou ask, blame thou not any man; and when thou hast asked, blame thou justly [or chastise thou rightly].
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:8  Before that thou hear, answer thou not a word; and in the midst of elder men add thou not to speak.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:9  Strive thou not, of (or in) that thing that dis-easeth [or grieveth] not thee; and stand thou not in the doom of sins [or (with) sinners].
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:10  Son, thy deeds be not in many things; and if thou art rich, thou shalt not be without part of guilt. For if thou pursuest [or shalt follow](after), thou shalt not [over]-take; and thou shalt not escape, if thou runnest before.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:11  There is a man travailing, and hast(en)ing, and sorrowing, and unpious; and by so much the more he shall not have plenty [or he shall not abound].
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:12  There is a man fade, that is, feeble, failing more than others, needy of recovering, failing more in virtue, and plenteous in poverty; and the eye of God beheld him in good, and raised him (up) from his lowness, [There is a man withered, needing recovering, more failing in virtue, and abounding in poorness; and the eye of God beheld him in good, and reared him (up) from his lowness;]
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:13  and enhanced his head; and many men wondered [or marvelled] in (or about) him, and honoured [or worshipped] God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:14  Goods and evils, that is, prosperities and adversities, life and death, poverty and honesty (or honours or riches), be of (or from) God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:15  Wisdom, and learning, and cunning (or knowing) of the law be with the Lord; love [or loving] and the ways of good men be at, [or with], (or from) him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:16  Error and darknesses be made together to (or with) sinners; forsooth they that make full out joy in evil, wax eld [or old] together into evils.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:17  The gift of God dwelleth to (or with) just [or rightwise] men; and (the) increasings of him shall have prosperities [into] without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:18  Some man there is made rich in doing scarcely [or (in) scarcely doing], and this is the part of his meed,
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:19  in that that he saith, I have found rest to (or for) me, and now I alone shall eat of my goods. And he know not that time passeth him, and death nigheth (or approacheth), and he shall leave all things to other men, and shall die [or and die].
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:20  Stand thou in thy testament, and speak thou (al)together in it; and wax thou eld [or old] in the work of thy behests (or of thy commands).
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:21  Dwell [or Abide] thou not in the works of sinners; but trust thou in God, and dwell in thy place. For it is easy in the eyes of God, suddenly to make honest (or rich) a poor man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:22  The blessing of God hast(en)eth into the meed of a just man [or the rightwise]; and the going forth of him maketh fruit in swift honour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:23  Say thou not, What is need to me (or What do I need)? and what goods (or good things) shall be (for) me hereafter?
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:24  Say thou not, I am sufficient, and what shall I be made worse hereafter?
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:25  In the day of goods (or good things), be thou not unmindful of evils, and in the day of evils, be thou not unmindful of goods (or good things); (On a good day do not forget the bad days, and on a bad day do not forget the good days;)
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:26  for it is easy before God to yield in the day of death, to each man after his ways.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:27  The malice of one hour maketh forgetting of most lechery; and in the end of a man is making naked of his works.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:28  Praise thou not any man before his death; for why a man is known in (or by) his sons.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:29  Bring thou not each man into thine house; for why many treasons be of a guileful man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:30  For why as the entrails of stinking things break out, and as a partridge is led into a trap, either (a) net, and as a capret is led into a snare, so and the heart of proud men; and as a behold-er seeing the fall of his neighbour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:31  For he turneth goods [or good things] into evils, and setteth treasons, and putteth a wem, (or a spot, or a blemish) on chosen men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:32  Fire is increased of a sparkle (or by a spark), and blood is increased of (or by) a guileful (or treacherous) man; for why a sinful man setteth treason [or waiteth] to (or lieth in wait for) blood.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:33  Take heed to thee from a guileful man, for he maketh [or forgeth] evils; lest peradventure he bring in on thee scorning without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 11:34  Receive thou an alien to thee, and he shall destroy thee in a whirl-wind, and he shall make thee alien (or alienated) from thine own ways.

ECCLESIASTICUS 12:3  It is not well to him that is customable [or is busy] in evils, and to him that giveth not alms; for why the Highest both hateth sinners, and doeth mercy to them that do penance.
ECCLESIASTICUS 12:4  Give thou to a merciful man [or to the merciful], and receive thou not a sinner, that is, (one) obstinate in sins; God shall yield vengeance both to unfaithful men and to sinners, keep-ing them in the day of vengeance. Give thou to a good man, and receive thou not a sinner.
ECCLESIASTICUS 12:5  Do thou good [or well] to a meek man, and give thou not to an unpious man, that is, (one) obstinate in sin; forbid thou (thyself) to give loaves to him, lest in those [or (with) them], he be(come) mightier than thou. What (or How) shall a caldron commune to (or with) a pot? for when those hurtle themselves together, the pot shall be broken.
ECCLESIASTICUS 13:3  A rich man shall do unjustly, and shall gnash, as ready yet to do worse; but a poor man hurt shall be still [or shall hold his peace].

ECCLESIASTICUS 13:5  If thou hast, he shall live together with thee, and shall make thee void; and he shall not have sorrow on thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 13:6  If thou art needful [or necessary] to him, he shall deceive [or beguile] thee; and he shall flatter, and shall give hope, telling to thee all goods (or every good thing); and shall say, What is need to thee [or What need is to thee]?
ECCLESIASTICUS 13:7  And he shall shame thee in his meats, till he annihilate or extinguish thee twice and thrice, and at the last he shall scorn thee; afterward he shall see, and shall forsake thee, and he shall move his head to (or at) thee. Be thou made meek to God, and abide thou his hands.

ECCLESIASTICUS 13:11  Withhold thou not to speak with him evenly, that is, speak thou to him without reverence, and believe thou not to his many words; for of (or with) much speech he shall tempt thee, and he shall laugh privily, and shall ask thee of (or about) thine hid things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 13:12  His cruel soul shall keep thy words, and he shall not spare of [or from] malice, and of [or from] bonds.

ECCLESIASTICUS 13:20  And as meekness is (an) abomi-nation to a proud man, so and a poor man is (an) abomination of (or to) a rich man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 13:21  A rich man moved, that is, disturbed, either hurled, is confirmed of (or by) his friends; but a meek man, when he falleth, shall be cast [or put] out, yea, of (his) known men (or by his friends).

ECCLESIASTICUS 15:3  It shall feed him with the bread of life, and of understanding; and it shall give drink to him with water of heal(th)ful [or of wholesome] wisdom;
ECCLESIASTICUS 15:4  it shall be made steadfast in him, and he shall not be bowed (or turned away)from the evenness of rightfulness. And it shall hold him, and he shall not be shamed [or confounded];
ECCLESIASTICUS 15:5  and it shall enhance him at (or it shall exalt him above) his neighbours. And in the midst of the church he [or it] shall open his mouth; and God shall fill him with the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, and shall clothe him with the stole of glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 15:6  God shall treasure on him mirth, and full out joying; and shall inherit him with (an) everlasting name.

ECCLESIASTICUS 15:8  for why it goeth away far from pride, and guile [or treachery]. Men leasing-mongers [or liars] shall not be mindful thereof, and soothfast men be found therein; and shall have pros-perity unto the beholding of God.

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:1  He that liveth without beginning and end, made (out) of nought all things together;

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:3  and he dwelleth a King unover-come [or unvanquished] without end.

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:5  But who shall tell out the virtue (or the strength) of his greatness? either [or] who shall lay to for to tell out his mercy?
ECCLESIASTICUS 18:6  It is not to make less, neither to lay to; neither it is to find the great things of God. [There is not to lessen, nor to add (to); nor there is to find the great worthy things of God.]

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:13  The merciful doing of man is about his neighbour; but the mercy of the Lord is over each [or upon all] flesh. He that hath mercy, and teach-eth, and chastiseth as a shepherd his flock,
ECCLESIASTICUS 18:14  do he mercy, taking the teaching of merciful doing; and he that hast(en)-eth in the dooms thereof [or of him].

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:17  Lo! whether a word is not above [or over] a good gift? but ever either is with a man justified [or a justified man].
ECCLESIASTICUS 18:18  A fool shall upbraid sharply [or shall give reproof]; and the gift of an untaught man maketh (the) eyes to fail.

ECCLESIASTICUS 18:24  Have thou mind of (or remember the) ire [or wrath] in the day of ending; and make thou in living [or conversation] the time of yielding.

ECCLESIASTICUS 21:1  Son, thou hast done sin? [or Son, hast thou sinned?] add thou (to it) not again; but beseech thou for the former sins, that those [or they] be forgiven to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:2  As from the face of a serpent [or a shadow adder] flee thou sins; and if thou nighest (or approachest) to them, those [or they] shall take thee. The teeth of a lion be(as) the teeth there-of, that slay the souls of men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:3  All wickedness is as a sharp sword on either side; health is not to the wound thereof [or of it].
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:4  Chidings and wrongs shall destroy chattel [or substance]; and an house that is over-rich, shall be destroyed by pride; so the chattel [or substance] of a proud man shall be drawn up by the root.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:5  The prayer of a poor man shall come from the mouth unto (the) ears of God; and doom shall come to him hastily.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:6  He that hateth reproving, is (in) a step of the sinner; and (or but) he that dreadeth God, shall be turned [or converted] to (him in) his heart.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:7  A mighty man with an hardy tongue is known afar; and a witty (or a witting or a knowing) man can or knoweth how to keep himself [or to slide] from that man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:8  He that buildeth his house with other men’s costs, is as he that gather-eth his stones in winter.

ECCLESIASTICUS 21:10  The way of sinners is set (al)to-gether [or planted] with stones; and in the end of them be hells , [or hell], and darknesses, and pains.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:11  He that keepeth rightfulness, shall hold the wit (or the understanding) thereof. The perfection of God’s dread is wisdom and wit.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:12  He shall not be taught, which is not wise in (what is) good. Forsooth unwisdom is, which is plenteous in evil; and wit is not, where (there) is bitterness. [He shall not be learned, that is not wise in good. There is forsooth unwisdom, that aboundeth in evil; and there is not wit, where is bitterness.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:13  The cunning, (or knowing, or the knowledge) of a wise man shall be plenteous as flowing (water); and the counsel of him dwelleth as a well of life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:14  The heart of a fool is as a broken vessel; and it shall not hold any wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:15  Whatever wise word a cunning (or a knowing) man heareth, he shall praise (it), and lay to (or add to it). A lecherous man heard (it), and it shall displease him; and he shall cast [or throw] it away behind his back.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:16  The telling of a fool is as a burden in (or on) the way; for why grace shall be found in (or on) the lips of a wise man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:17  The mouth of a prudent man is sought in the church; and men shall think (on) his words in their hearts.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:18  As an house destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool; and the cunning (or the knowing) of an unwise man is words that may not be or be not able to be told out [or (that be) untellable].
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:19  Stocks in (or on) the feet is teach-ing [or doctrine] to a fool; and as bonds of hands on the right hand.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:20  A fool enhanceth his voice in laughing; but a wise man shall laugh scarcely still.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:21  Teaching is a golden ornament to a prudent man; and as an ornament of the arm [or an arm-circle] in (or on) the right arm.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:22  The foot of a fool is light (or easily) into the house of a neighbour; and a wise man shall be ashamed of the person of a mighty man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:23  A fool beholdeth from the window into the house; but a learned man shall stand withoutforth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:24  It is folly of a man to harken by the door; and a prudent man shall be grieved by despising [or with strife].
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:25  The lips of unprudent men shall tell fond things [or follies]; but the words of prudent men shall be weigh-ed in a balance.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:26  The heart of fools is in their mouth; and the mouth of wise men is in their heart.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:27  When a wicked man curseth the devil, he curseth his own soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 21:28  A privy backbiter shall defoul his soul, and in all things he shall be hated, and he that dwelleth, shall be hated; a still man and wise shall be honoured.

ECCLESIASTICUS 22:11  Weep thou on (or for) a dead man, for why his light [or the light of him] failed; and weep thou on (or for) a fool, for he failed of wit. Weep thou a little on (or for) a dead man, for he hath rested. Forsooth the life of a full wicked man is full wicked, more than the death of a fool.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:12  The mourning of (or for) a dead man is seven days; but the mourning of (or for) a fool and of (or for) a wick-ed man is all the days of their life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:13  Speak thou not much with a fool, and go thou not with an unwise man. Keep thee from him, (so) that thou have not dis-ease [or grief]; and thou shalt not be defouled in the sin of him. Bow thou away from him, and thou shalt find rest; and be thou not annoyed (or harmed) by his folly.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:14  What shall be made heavier than lead? and what other name than a fool is to it [or to him]?
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:15  It is lighter (or easier) to bear gravel, and salt, and a gobbet of iron, than a man unprudent [or an impru-dent man], and a fool, and unfaithful.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:16  As an heap [or (a) joining] of trees, bound together in the foundament of the building, shall not be unbound [or unloosed], so and an heart confirmed in the thought of counsel.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:17  The thought of a wise man shall not be made shrewd (or depraved) in any time, neither dreaded.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:18  As chaffs in high places, and sand without meddling of him [or and mor-tar without due cost], set against the face of the wind, shall not dwell; so and a dreadful heart in the thought [or in the thinking] of a fool against-standeth not against the fierceness of dread. As adorning, either pargeting, full of gravel in a clear wall, so and a fearedful heart in the thought of a fool [or the trembling heart in the thinking of a fool] shall not dread in any time; so and he that dwelleth ever[more] in the behests (or the commands) of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:19  He that pricketh the eye, shall lead out tears; and he that pricketh the heart, bringeth forth wit.

ECCLESIASTICUS 22:21  Though thou bringest forth a sword to a friend, despair thou not; for there is going again to the friend.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:22  If he openeth a sorrowful mouth, dread thou not; for why there is according, except (for) despising, and shame, and pride, and showing [or opening] of private(s), (or of secrets), and a treacherous wound; in all these things a friend shall fly [or flee] away.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:23  Have thou faith with a friend in his poverty, (so) that thou be glad also in his goods. In the time of his tribulations, dwell thou [or abide still] faithful to him, (so) that also thou be even-heir in the heritage of him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:24  Heat and smoke of fire is made high before the fire of a chimney; so and cursings, and despisings, and menaces, [or curses, and wrongs, and threats], come before blood.

ECCLESIASTICUS 22:26  (even) though [or and if] evils come to me by him, I shall suffer. Each man that shall hear, shall keep warily himself from him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 22:27  Who shall give keeping to (or keep watch over) my mouth, and a certain sealing on my lips, (so) that I fall not by those, and that my tongue lose (or destroy) not me? ECCLESIASTICUS 23:1  Lord, Father, and lordly governor of my life, forsake thou me not in the thought [or the thinking] and (the) counsel of them, that is, of fools and unfaithful men; neither suffer (or allow) thou me to fall in that shame.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:2  Who setteth above in my thought(s) beatings, and in mine heart the teaching of wisdom, that in the uncunnings, (or unknowings, or ignorances) of them he spare not me, and that the trespasses of them appear not? [Who putteth upon in my thinking scourges, and in mine heart doctrine of wisdom, that to the unknowings of them he spare not to me, and appear not the guilts of them?]
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:3  Lest mine uncunnings, (or my unknowings, or ignorances) increase, and my trespasses be multiplied, and my sins be plenteous [or abound]; and lest I fall in the sight of mine adversaries, and mine enemy have joy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:4  Lord, Father, and God of my life, forsake thou not me in the thought(s) of them. Give thou not to me enhancing of mine eyes, yea, suffer not (or do not allow) that pride be lord over me;
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:5  and turn thou away from me all shrewd (or depraved) desire.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:6  Do thou away from me the covetousnesses of the womb, and the covetousnesses of lechery [or of lust] take me not; and give thou not me (over)(in)to a soul unreverent and undiscreet or unsavoury.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:7  Sons, hear ye the teaching of (the) mouth; and he that keepeth it, shall not perish by his lips, neither shall be caused to stumble in worst works.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:8  A sinner and proud man shall be taken [or caught] in his vanity; and a cursed man shall be caused to stumble in those [or in them].
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:9  Thy mouth be not customable (or accustomed) to swearing; for why many fallings be therein. [To swearing use not thy mouth; many forsooth fallings be in it.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:10  Forsooth the naming of God be not customable [or continual] in thy mouth, and be thou not meddled to, [or mingled, (or mixed with)] the names of saints; for thou shalt not be guiltless of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:11  For as a servant that is asked busily, shall not want (or lack) wan-ness, [or envy]; so each man swearing and naming shall not be purged of sin in all. A man swearing much shall be filled with wickedness; and venge-ance shall not go away from his house. And if he deceiveth a brother, his trespass shall be above [or upon] him; and if he feigneth, he shall trespass doubly [or double]. And if he sweareth in vain, he shall not be justified; for why his house shall be filled with worst yielding.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:12  Also again-ward another speech is into death; be it not found in the heritage of Jacob. For why all these things shall be done away from merciful men; and they shall not delight in trespasses.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:13  Thy mouth be not customable (or accustomed) to unreverent speech; for why a word of sin is in it. [To the undisciplined speech use not thy mouth; forsooth there is in it the word of sin.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:14  Have thou mind on (or Think upon) thy father and mother; for (or when) thou standest in the midst of great men. Lest peradventure God forget thee in the sight of them; and lest thou made a fool by thus customableness [or busyness], suffer shame, either scorning, [or reproof], and haddest rather to be not born, and curse the day of thy birth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:15  A man customable in (or accustomed to using) the words of shame [or reproof], in all (his) days shall not be taught.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:16  Two kinds be plenteous [or abound] in sins, and the third bring-eth ire and perdition. An hot soul burn-ing as fire shall not be quenched, till it swallow something; and a wicked man in the mouth of his flesh shall not fail, till he kindle (a) fire.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:17  Each bread is sweet to a lecher-ous man; he shall not be made weary, trespassing till to the end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:18  Each man that passeth [or that over-goeth] his bed, doeth despite against his soul, and saith, Who seeth me? Darknesses (en)compass me, and (the) walls cover me, and no man behold-eth me. Whom dread I? The Highest shall not have mind on my sins.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:19  And he understandeth not, that the eye of him, that is, of God, seeth all things; for why the dread of such a man putteth away from him(self) the dread of God, and the eyes of men that dread him put away from him God’s dread. And he knew not, that the eyes of the Lord be much more clearer than the sun, and behold all the ways of men, and the depth of the sea, and they behold the hearts of men into hid parts.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:20  For why all things were known to the Lord, before that they were made [or formed](out) of nought; so and after the making, he beholdeth all things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:21  This man shall be punished in the streets of the city; he shall be driven away as an horse colt, and he shall be taken [or caught], where he hopeth not. And he shall be shame to all men; for he understood not the dread of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:22  So and each woman forsaking her husband shall do sin, and ordaining heritage, that is, (an) heir of her husband, of (or by) an alien matrimony.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:23  For first she was unbelieveful in the law of the Highest, and the second time she forsook her husband; and the third time she was defouled in adultery, and ordained to him sons of (or by) another man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:24  She, this woman, shall be brought into the church, and men shall behold on her sons.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:25  Her sons shall not give [or take] roots, and her branches shall not give fruit.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:26  They shall leave the mind (or the memory) of her into cursing, and the shame of her shall not be done away.
ECCLESIASTICUS 23:27  And they that be left shall know, that nothing is better than the dread of God, and nothing is sweeter than to behold in the commandments of the Lord.

ECCLESIASTICUS 24:4  I dwelled in highest things, and my throne (is) in a pillar of [a] cloud.
ECCLESIASTICUS 24:5  I alone went about the compass [or the circle] of heaven, and I pierced the depth of the sea;
ECCLESIASTICUS 24:6  and I went in the waves of the sea, and I stood in (or on) all the land [or all (the) earth]. And I had the first dignity in each people, and in each folk; and I trod by virtue (or power) on the necks of all excellent men and meek [or all high and low];

ECCLESIASTICUS 24:11  and in like manner I rested in a city hallowed, and my power was in Jerusalem. [and in an hallowed city (in) like manner I rested, and in Jerusalem (was) my power.]

ECCLESIASTICUS 25:11  The dread of God hath set itself above [or over] all things. Blessed is the man to whom it is given to have the dread of God; to whom shall he be likened, that holdeth that dread?
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:12  The dread of God is the beginning of his love; forsooth the beginning of faith is to be fast-joined thereto [or to him].
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:13  The sorrow of (the) heart is each wound; and the wickedness of a woman is all malice . A leech (or A physician) shall see each wound, and (or but) not the wound of (the) heart; and all wickedness, and (or but) not the wickedness of a woman;
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:14  and each covering [or all hid thing], that is, (the) colouring of malice, and not the covering [or the hid thing] of haters; and each [or all] vengeance, and not the vengeance of enemies.

ECCLESIASTICUS 25:17  The wickedness of a woman changeth her face; and she blinded her cheer (or her face) as a bear doeth, and she shall show as a sack(cloth) in the midst of (her) neighbours.

ECCLESIASTICUS 25:20  As a going-up (or an ascent) full of gravel in (or to) the feet of an eld [or old] man, so is a woman (that is) a great jangler to a peaceable [or quiet] man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:21  Behold thou not the fairness of a woman, and covet thou not a woman for (her) fairness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:22  The ire and unreverence of a woman to her husband is a great shame (or reproof). If a woman hath the first dignity [or (the) mastery], either chief governail, she is contrary to her husband.
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:23  A low heart, and (a) sorrowful face, and (a) wound of death, is(from) a wicked woman. Feeble hands and knees unbound, (resulteth from) a woman that blesseth not her husband.
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:24  The beginning of sin was made of (or by) a woman; and all we die by her.
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:25  Give thou not issue to thy water, yea, not a little issue; neither to a wicked woman freedom, [or leave], of going forth [or going out].
ECCLESIASTICUS 25:26  If she goeth not at thine hand, she shall shame thee in the sight of (thine) enemies. Cut her away from thy fleshes, lest ever[more] she mis-use thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:1  The husband of a good woman is blessed; for why the number of their years is double [or the number for-sooth of the years of him double].
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:2  A strong woman, that is, against sins, delighteth her husband; and (he) shall [ful] fill in peace the years of his life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:3  A good woman is a good part (or partner); in the good part of them that dread God, she shall be given to a man for [his] good deeds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:4  Forsooth (if) the heart of a rich man and (or) of a poor man is good; in all time their cheer (or his face)is glad.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:5  Mine heart dreaded of three things, and my face dreaded [or was afeared] in (or of) the fourth thing. Betraying of a city, and the gathering together of people, that is, in conspiring of the people against the prince, and false challenge; all (these) things (be more) grievous on (or worse than) death.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:6  The sorrow of heart, and mourn-ing, is a jealous woman. In a jealous woman is(a) beating [or scourge] of (the) tongue, and she communeth with all men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:7  As a yoke of oxes [or oxen] which is moved, so and a wicked woman; he that holdeth her, is as he that taketh [or caught](hold of) a scorpion.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:8  A drunken woman is great ire, and despising [or strife]; and her filth-(hood)[or nakedness] shall not be covered.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:9  The fornication of a woman is in the raising of (her) eyes; and [she] shall be known in (or by) the eyelids of her.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:10  Make thou firm the keeping in (or of) a daughter not turning away her-self; lest she mis-use herself, if she findeth (an) occasion.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:11  Be thou ware of all unreverence of her eyes; and wonder thou not, if she despiseth thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:12  As a way-goer thirsting shall open the mouth at a well, and shall drink of each water next; and the foresaid daughter shall sit against each pale, and shall open the arrow case against each arrow [or against all arrow(s) shall open the quiver], till she fail.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:13  The grace of a busy woman shall delight her husband; and shall make fat his bones.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:14  The cunning (or the knowing) of her is the gift of God. A wise woman and a still (one) is not (ex)changing of (or with) a learned [or the taught] soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:15  Grace [up] on grace is an holy woman, and shamefast. Forsooth all weighing is not worth a continent soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:16  As the sun rising in the world in the highest things of God, so the fairness of a good woman is into the ornament, or the adornment, of her house.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:17  A lantern shining on an holy candlestick, and the fairness of a face on (or in)[the] steadfast age, that is, as such a lantern lighteneth the church, and such a face maketh fair ripe age, so a good woman maketh fair her house.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:18  Golden pillars on silvern founda-ments (or foundations), and steadfast feet on the soles of a steadfast [or a stable] woman. Everlasting founda-ments on a firm stone, and the behests, (or the commands), [or the commandments] of God in the heart of an holy woman.
