ECCLESIASTICUS 26:28  In two things mine heart was made sorry [or is made sorrowful], and in the third thing wrathfulness came to me. A man warrior failing by neediness, and a wise man despised. And God hath made him ready to (or for) the sword, that passeth over [or over-goeth] from rightfulness [or rightwiseness] to sin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 26:29  Two species appeared hard and perilous to me; a merchant is deliver-ed of hard from his negligence, and a taverner shall not be justified of [or from](the) sins of lips.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:1  Many men have trespassed for neediness; and he that seeketh to be made rich, turneth away his eye.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:2  As a stake [or a pale] is fastened in the midst of a heap [or a joining] of stones, so and a man shall be anguished by sins betwixt the midst of selling and buying. Trespass shall be all-broken with him that trespasseth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:3  If thou holdest not thee diligently in the dread of the Lord, thine house shall soon be turned upside down.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:4  As dust shall dwell in the holes of a riddle, so the anguish of a man shall dwell in the thought(s) of him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:5  A furnace proveth the vessels of a potter; and the temptation of tribu-lation proveth just [or rightwise] men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:6  As churl-like travail [or earth-working] about a tree showeth the fruit thereof, so a word of thought showeth the heart of man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:7  Praise thou not a man before a word fully ended; for why this is the temptation, that is, (the) proving, of men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:8  If thou pursuest rightfulness [or followest rightwiseness], thou shalt take it; thou shalt clothe it as a long cloth, (or a cloak), [or an aube] of honour, and thou shalt dwell with it, and it shall defend thee without end, and in the day of knowing thou shalt find steadfastness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:9  Volatiles [or Fowls] come together to birds like themselves; and truth shall (re)turn again to them that work it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:10  (As) a lion setteth espies [or wait-eth (or lieth in wait)] ever[more] to hunting; so sins to them that work wickedness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:11  An holy man dwelleth in wisdom, as the sun dwelleth; for why a fool is changed as the moon.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:12  In the midst of unwise men keep thou a word to (the) time; but be thou busy in the midst of them that think (upon) the law of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:13  The telling of sinners is hateful; and the laughing of them is in the trespasses of sin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:14  Speech swearing much shall make (for) standing up of hairs, for astonishing, to the head; and unrever-ence thereof [or (the) irreverence of it] is stopping of (the) ears.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:15  The shedding out of blood is in the chiding [or jangling] of proud men; and the cursing of them is grievous hearing, for in their chiding they blaspheme God often, and it is full grievous to faithful ears to hear such blasphemy of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:16  He that showeth openly the privates (or the secrets) of a friend, loseth (or destroyeth) faithfulness; and he shall not find a friend to his soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:17  Love thou a neighbour, and be thou joined with him in faith. For (or But) if thou showest openly the privates (or the secrets) of him, thou shalt not perfectly pursue after him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:18  For as a man that loseth his friend, so he that loseth the friendship of his neighbour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:19  And as a man that letteth go a bird from [or out of] his hand, so thou that hast forsaken thy neighbour, and thou shalt not take (or get) him (again).
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:20  Thou shalt not pursue [or follow] him, for he is far absent [or far he is away]; for he escaped as a capret from a snare, for the soul of him is wounded.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:21  Thou shalt no more be able to bind him together; but of (or after) evil saying is according. Soothly to show openly the privates (or the secrets) of a friend, is despair of a soul unblessed [or unfaithful].
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:22  He that twinkleth with the eye, maketh [or forgeth] wicked things; and no man shall cast him away.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:23  In the sight of thine eyes he shall defoul his mouth, and he shall wonder on thy words; but at the last he shall turn waywardly [or pervert] his mouth, and in his word he shall give slander [or in (or regarding) thy words he shall give slander].
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:24  I [have] heard many things, that is, evils, and I made (them) not even to him, yea, I areckoned not another malice even to the malice of this man; and the Lord shall hate him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:25  If a man casteth a stone on high it shall fall on his (own) head; and the guileful wound of a guileful [or treach-erous] man shall part wounds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:26  And he that diggeth a ditch, shall fall into it; and he that setteth a stone to a neighbour, shall offend therein [or shall stumble in it]; and he that setteth a snare to another man, shall perish therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:27  If a man maketh worst [or wicked] counsel, it shall be turned [up] on him; and he shall not know from whence it shall come to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:28  The scorning and despising of proud men and vengeance shall set espy to him, as a lion doeth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:29  They that delight in the fall of just [or rightwise] men, shall perish by a snare; forsooth sorrow shall waste them, before that they die.
ECCLESIASTICUS 27:30  Ire [or Wrath] and madness or rage, ever either be abominable; and a sinful man shall hold those [or them].
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:1  He that will be avenged, shall find of (or from) the Lord vengeance; and he keeping shall keep his sins to be punished harder by his rightfulness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:2  Forgive thou to thy neighbour that annoyeth (or harmeth) thee, and then (thy) sins shall be released [or be forgiven] to thee (after) praying.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:3  A man keepeth ire [or wrath] to (or for a) man; and seeketh he of (or from) God medicine (or remedy)?
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:4  He hath no mercy on a man like himself; and (yet) beseecheth he the Highest for his own sins?
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:5  He the while he is flesh, reserveth ire; and asketh he of God mercy? who shall pray for his sins?
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:6  Have thou mind on the [or thy] last things, and cease thou [or leave (off)] to be (anyone’s) enemy. For why failing and death nigh not in the commandments of God, [or Rotten-ness forsooth and death, stand on in the behests of him].
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:7  Have thou mind on [or Remem-ber] the dread of the Lord, and be not wroth to the neighbour. Have thou mind on the testament of the Highest, and despise thou the ignorance of thy neighbour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:8  Abstain thee from strife, and thou shalt decrease, either abridge, (thy) sins. For why a wrathful man kindleth strife;
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:9  and a sinful man, that is, a sower of discords, shall disturb (or shall trouble) friends, and he shall send in enmity in the midst of men having peace.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:10  For why after the trees of the wood, so [the] fire shall burn on high; and after the might of a man, so his wrathfulness shall be, and after his chattel [or his substance] he shall enhance his ire.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:11  Hasty striving [or An hasted strife] shall kindle fire, and hasty chiding shall shed out blood; and a tongue bearing witnessing shall bring death.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:12  If thou blowest, as fire it shall burn on high; and if thou spittest thereon, it shall be quenched; ever either, that is, a word kindling ire, and a word refraining it, come forth (out) of the mouth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:13  A privy backbiter, and a double-tongued man, yea, he that speaketh fair before a man, and evil behind him, is cursed; for he disturbed (or troubled) many men having peace.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:14  The third tongue hath stirred many men, and hath scattered them from folk into folk. It hath destroyed walled cities of rich men, and hath mined down (or undermined) the houses of great men. It hath cut down the virtues of peoples, and hath unknit strong folks.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:15  The third tongue hath cast out wedded, or honest, women, and hath (de)prived them of their travails.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:16  He that beholdeth the third tongue, shall not have rest; neither shall have a friend, in whom he shall rest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:17  The wound of [a] beating maketh wanness; but the wound of (the) tongue shall make less [or break] the bones.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:18  Many men fell down by the sharp-ness of (the) sword; but not so (many), (or not as many) as they that perished [or died] by their tongue.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:19  He is blessed that is covered from a wicked, [or shrewd, (or depraved)] tongue; and he that passed not in the wrathfulness thereof, and he that drew not the yoke thereof, and was not bound in the bonds thereof.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:20  For why the yoke thereof is an iron yoke, and the bond thereof is a brazen bond.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:21  The death thereof is the worst death; and hell is more profitable, that is, the pain of hell is less evil, then it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:22  The perseverance thereof shall not dwell, but it shall hold the ways of unjust men; in his flame it shall not burn just [or rightwise] men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:23  They that forsake God, shall fall into it; and it shall burn greatly in them, and it shall not be quenched; and as a lion it shall be sent into them, and as a (leo)pard it shall hurt them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:24  Beset thine ears with thorns, and do not thou hear a wicked tongue; and make thou doors to (or for) thy mouth, and locks to (or for) thine ears. Well thou [or melt together], or temper thou, thy gold, and thy silver;
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:25  and make thou a balance to (or for) thy words, and rightful bridles to (or for) thy mouth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 28:26  And take heed, lest peradventure thou slide in (or with thy) tongue, and fall in the sight of enemies, set-ting treason, [or waiting, (or lying in wait)] to (or for) thee, and thy fall be uncurable [or unhealable] into death.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:1  He that doeth mercy, lendeth to his neighbour; and he that is full mighty in hand, keepeth the commandments.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:2  Lend thou to thy neighbour in the time of his need; and again yield thou to a neighbour in his time.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:3  Confirm thou a word, and do thou faithfully with him; and in all time thou shalt find that, that is needful to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:4  Many men guessed borrowing as finding, and gave dis-ease [or grief] to those men that helped them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:5  Till they take (or receive), they kiss the hands of the giver; and in promises they make meek their voice. And in (or at) the time of yielding, he shall ask (for more) time, [or delay-ing], and he shall speak words of annoy(ance), (or of hurt), and of grutchings (or grumblings), and he shall challenge falsely, [or plead (for), or complain (about)] the time, to tarry the paying of (the) debt.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:6  Forsooth if he may yield, he shall be adversary [or enemy]; of a shilling scarcely he shall yield the half [or scarcely of the whole he shall yield the half], and he shall reckon that as (re)funding. Else he shall defraud him in (or of) his money, and the lender shall have him (as) an enemy without cause. And he shall yield to him, that is, to the lender, wrongs and cursings; and for honour and benefice, he shall yield to him despising.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:7  Many men lend not, not for cause of wickedness, but they dreaded to be defrauded without cause [or will-fully].
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:8  Nevertheless on (or for) a meek man in soul, that is, a full poor debtor, be thou stronger; and for alms-[deed(s)] draw thou not him (along).
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:9  For the commandment of God take (or receive) thou a poor man; and for his neediness leave thou not him void (or do not let him go away empty-handed).
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:10  Lose thou money for a brother and friend, and hide thou not it under a stone, into perdition.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:11  Put thy treasure in the command-ments of the Highest; and it shall profit to thee more than gold.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:12  (En)close thou alms in the bosom of a poor man; and this alms shall pray for thee to be delivered of (or by) God from all evil. The alms of a man is as a bag [or a little sack] with him; and it shall keep the grace of [a] man, that is, God’s grace, given to man, as the apple of the eye. And afterward it shall rise again, and shall yield to them a yielding, to each man into (or onto) the head of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:13  Above [or Over (or Better than)] the shield of a mighty man, and above [or over (or better than)] a spear it shall fight against thine enemy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:14  A good man maketh faith to (or for) his neighbour in becoming (a) borrow (er), (or a guarantor), for him in need; and he that loseth, shall leave shame to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:15  Forget thou not the grace of the borrower (or of the guarantor); for he gave his life for thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:16  A sinful man [or The sinner] and unclean fleeth the promiser. A sinner areckoneth to himself the good words of the borrower (or of the guarantor);
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:17  and the unkind man in wit forsaketh a man delivering him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:18  A man promiseth for his neighbour; and when he hath lost reverence, that is, shamefastness before God and man, the borrower shall be forsaken of (or by) him. Worst [or Most shrewd (or depraved)] promise, by which the neighbour promised falsely to deliver his borrow, hath lost [or spoiled] many loving men, and hath moved them as the waves of the sea. It going in compass made mighty men to pass over [or to go out (or to go away)]; and (then) they wandered about among alien folks.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:19  A sinner breaking [or overpass-ing] the commandment of the Lord shall fall into a wicked promise; and he that endeavoureth to do many things, shall fall into doom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:20  Recover thy neighbour by thy virtue (or according to thy power); and take heed to thyself, lest thou fall (in the same manner).
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:21  The beginning of (the) life of a man is water, and bread, and clothing, and (a) house covering filth-[hood](or nakedness).
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:22  Better is the lifelode (or the liveli-hood) of a poor man under the cover-ing of spars, than [plenteous] shining feasts in pilgrimage without (a) house,
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:23  The least thing pleaseth thee for a great thing, and thou shalt not hear the shame [or reproof] of pilgrimage.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:24  It is(a) wicked life to seek harbour from house into house; and where he shall be harboured, he shall not do trustily, neither he shall open the mouth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:25  He shall be harboured, and he shall feed, and give drink to unkind men; and yet he shall hear bitter things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:26  Pass, thou that art harboured, [or Go, guest], and array a table; and give thou meats to other men, (of) those things that thou hast in the hand.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:27  Go thou out from the face of the honour of my friends, for the friend-ship, either affinity, of mine house [or for (the) need of mine house]; by harbouring thou art made a brother to me.
ECCLESIASTICUS 29:28  These things be grievous to a man having wit; the reproving of house, and the despising of the usurer [or the lender].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:1  He that loveth his son, giveth busily beatings to him, (so) that he be glad in his last thing, and (so) that the son touch not the doors of neighbours.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:2  He that teacheth his son, shall be praised in (or for) him; and shall have glory in him in the midst of (his) menials.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:3  He that teacheth his son, sendeth the enemy into envy; and in the midst of friends he shall have glory in that son.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:4  (And though) The father of him is dead, and (yet) he is as not dead; for he hath left after him a son like him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:5  He saw in his life, and was glad in (or over) him; and in his death he was not sorry [or sorrowed not], neither was ashamed before (his) enemies.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:6  For he left a defender of the house against (his) enemies; and (one) yielding grace to (his) friends.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:7  For defending the souls (or the lives) of his sons, he shall bind together his wounds; and his entrails [or the bowels of him] shall be disturbed (or troubled) on each voice.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:8  An horse untamed, either unchastised, shall escape hard, and a son unchastised shall escape heady (or become headstrong).
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:9  Flatter thou the son, and he shall make thee dreading; play thou with him, and he shall make thee sorry [or sorrow(ful)].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:10  Laugh thou not with him of (or about) his follies, lest thou have sorrow together, and at the last thy teeth shall be astonished.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:11  Give thou not power to him in youth, and despise thou not his thoughts.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:12  Bow thou (down) his neck in youth, and beat thou his sides, while he is a young child; lest peradventure he wax hard [or inwardly harden], and believe not to thee, and he shall be (a) sorrow of (or to thy) soul to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:13  Teach thy son, and work in him; lest thou offend into the filth of him (or lest his filthy behaviour offend thee).
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:14  Better is a poor man whole, and strong in mights [or strengths], than a rich man feeble, and beaten with malice.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:15  The health of (the) soul (or of the body)is in the holiness of rightfulness [or rightwiseness], and it is better than any gold and silver; and a strong body is better than full much chattel [or than money without measure].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:16  No chattel is above the chattel of (the) health of (the) body; and no liking is above the joy of (the) heart. [There is not money over the money of the health of (the) body; and there is not liking over the joy of (the) heart.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:17  Better is death than (a) bitter life, and everlasting rest is better than sickness dwelling continually [or enduring].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:18  Goods hid in a closed mouth be as settings forth of meats set about a sepulchre.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:19  What shall sacrifice profit to an idol? for why it shall not eat, neither shall smell. So he that is driven away from the Lord,
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:20  and beareth the meeds (or rewards) of wickedness, [or of shrewdness, (or of depravity)], seeing with eyes, and wailing inwardly, as a gelding embracing a virgin [or a maiden], and sighing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:21  Give thou not sorrow to thy soul, that is, unreasonable sorrow, that annoyeth (or harmeth) both body and soul, and torment not thyself in (or with) thy (own) counsel, as they do that despair through sorrow, and then slay themselves.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:22  Mirth of heart, this is the life of man, and is(a) treasure of holiness without failing; and full out joying of a man is long life [or long living].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:23  Have thou mercy on thy soul, and please thou God; and hold together and gather together thine heart in the holiness of him, and put far away sorrow from thee. For why sorrow hath slain many men; and none health is therein [or there is not profit in it].
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:24  Envy and wrathfulness shall make (for) less days [or Envy and wrath shall lessen days]; and thoughts shall bring eldness before the time.
ECCLESIASTICUS 30:25  A shining [or bright] heart is good in meats, (or for meals or digestion); for why meats thereof be made diligently.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:1  Waking of honesty shall make fleshes to fail, (or Waiting for, or Watching over riches shall make the flesh to pine away); and (the much) thought thereof shall take away sleep.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:2  Thought(s) of before-knowing turn-eth away wit; and grievous sickness maketh sober the soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:3  A rich man travailed in the gather-ing of (his) chattel [or (his) substance]; and in his rest he shall be filled with his goods.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:4  A poor man travailed in (the) decreasing [or the less(en)ing] of (his) lifelode; and in the end he is made needy. (A poor man worked hard, even though his livelihood continued to decrease; and in the end, he is still needy.)
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:5  He that loveth gold, shall not be justified; and he that pursueth [or followeth](after) wasting (or corrup-tion), shall be [full]-filled thereof.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:6  Many men be given into the fallings of gold, that is, many men felled into sins for gold; and the perdition [or the loss] of them was made in the fairness thereof [or of it].
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:7  A tree of offension, (or of offence, or a stumbling block), is the gold of them that make sacrifice; woe to them that pursue [or follow] it, and each unprudent man shall perish therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:8  Blessed is a rich man, which is found without wem of covetousness and avarice; and that went not after gold, neither hoped in money, and treasures.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:9  Who is this, and we shall praise him? for he did marvels in his life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:10  Which [or Who] is proved, (or tried, or tested) therein [or in (or by) it], and is found perfect, and ever-lasting glory shall be to him? which might trespass, and trespassed not, and do evils, and did not.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:11  Therefore his goods be estab-lished in the Lord; and all the church of saints shall tell out his alms-deeds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:12  Thou hast set at a great board (or a bountiful table); open thou not first thy cheek on it, that is, begin thou not to eat first. [And] Say thou not, whether those be many things, that be on it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:13  Have thou mind (or Remember), that an evil eye is (a) wayward, [or shrewd, (or depraved)](thing). What thing worse, than an eye is made? therefore of all his face he (or it) shall weep, when he seeth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:14  Stretch thou not forth first thine hand; and thou defouled by envy, be ashamed. Be thou not oppressed of (or by) wine in a feast.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:15  Understand of thyself the things, that be of thy neighbour. [Understand what be of thy neighbour, of thyself.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:16  Use thou as a discreet and temperate man these things that be set forth to thee; and (so) be thou not hated, when thou eatest (too) much.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:17  Cease thou first because of learn-ing, either nurture; and do not thou be outrageous [or do thou not be too much], lest peradventure thou offend.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:18  And if thou hast set in the midst of many men, stretch not forth [or not stretch thou out] thine hand sooner than they; and ask thou not first for to drink.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:19  A little wine is full(y) sufficient to a learned man; and in sleeping thou shalt not travail for that wine, and thou shalt not feel travail.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:20  Waking, and choler, either bitter moisture, and gnawing [or anguish] to an undiscreet and untemperate man. But the sleep of health is in a scarce (or a moderate) man; he shall sleep unto the morrowtide; and his soul (or his body) shall delight with him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:21  And if thou art constrained in eating [too] much, rise thou from the midst, and spew thou; and it shall refresh thee, and thou shalt not bring sickness to thy body.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:22  Son, hear thou me, and despise thou not me; and at the last thou shalt find (that) my words (be true). In all thy works be thou swift; and all sickness shall not come to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:23  The lips of many men shall bless a shining man in loaves; and the witnessing of his truth is faithful.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:24  The city shall grutch (or grumble) in the worst bread; and the witness-ing of wickedness thereof is sooth (or true).
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:25  Do not thou excite [or stir (up)] them that be diligent [or busy] in (or with) wine; for why wine hath destroyed many men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:26  Fire proveth hard iron; so wine drunken in drunkenness shall reprove the hearts of proud men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:27  Even life to men is wine drunken in soberness; if thou drinkest it meas-urably, thou shalt be sober. What is the life which is made less by wine? What defraudeth life? death. Wine was made in gladness, not in drunken-ness, at [or from] the beginning.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:28  Wine drunken measurably is full out joying of soul and of body. Sober drink is (the) health of (the) soul and of (the) body.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:29  Wine drunken much maketh voiding, and ire [or wrath], and many fallings, or mischiefs.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:30  Wine drunken much is bitterness of (the) soul. Strength of drunkenness and hurting of an unprudent man maketh virtue less, and making wounds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 31:31  In the feast of wine, reprove thou not a neighbour; and despise thou not him in his mirth. Say thou not words of shame [or of reproof] to him; and oppress thou not him in [again]-asking.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:1  They have set thee a governor, do not thou be enhanced (or exalted); be thou among them as one of them. Have thou (the) care of them, and so behold thou; and when all thy care is filled, sit thou to meat [or (to) rest].
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:2  That thou be glad for them, and take the ornament of grace; and get (a) crown, and (the) dignity of (the) congregation (or assembly).
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:3  Speak thou, the greater man in birth; for why the word of him that loveth cunning, (or knowing, or knowl-edge) become thee first; and hinder thou not (the) music.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:4  Where hearing is not, shed [or pour] thou not out a word; and do not thou be enhanced uncovenably (or inopportunely) in thy wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:5  A gem of carbuncle in the ornament of gold; and comparison of musics in the feast of wine.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:6  As in the making [or (the) forging] of gold is a signet of smaragdus (or emerald), so the number of musics is in merry and measurable [or temper-ate] wine.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:7  Hear thou [(while) being] still, and good grace shall come to thee for reverence. Young man, speak thou scarcely in (or for) thy cause, (only) when need is. If thou art asked twice, the head have thine answer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:8  In many things be thou as uncunning (or as unknowing), and hear thou [(while) being] still (al)to-gether, and asking [or seeking].
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:9  And presume thou not to speak in the midst of great men; and where eld [or old] men be, speak thou not much.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:10  Lightning shall go before hail, and grace shall go before shamefastness, and good grace shall come to thee for reverence.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:11  And in the hour of rising, trifle thee not, that is, make thee no tarrying in arraying, either trifling of hairs, as women do; forsooth run thou before first into thine house, and there call thou thee to answer[or and there be thou called to], and there play thou.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:12  And do thy conceits [or thy conceivings], that is, perform thy good purpose conceived there, and not in sins, and in a proud word.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:13  On all these things, bless thou the Lord, that made thee, and filling thee greatly of (or with) all his goods.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:14  He that dreadeth God, shall take his teaching; and they that wake to him, shall find blessing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:15  He that seeketh the law, shall be filled thereof; and he that doeth traitorously, shall be caused to stumble therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:16  They that dread God, shall find just doom; and shall kindle rightful-ness [or rightwisenesses] as (a) light.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:17  A sinful man, that is, obstinate in sin, shall eschew blaming [or shall shun correction]; and after his will (or according to his desire), he shall find comparison.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:18  A man of counsel shall not lose [or destroy] understanding; (but) a man alien and proud shall not dread dreading. Yea, after that he hath done with that dread without counsel, and he shall be reproved by his pursuings [or his followings].
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:19  Son, do thou nothing without counsel; and after the deed thou shalt not repent.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:20  Go thou not in the way of falling, and offend (or stumble) thou not against (the) stones [or and thou shalt not offend (or stumble) against (the) stones].
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:21  Betake thou not thee to a travail-ous way, lest thou set slander to thy soul (or thou cause thy own soul to stumble);
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:22  and be thou ware of thy sons, and perceive thou [or take heed] of thy menials.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:23  In all thy work believe thou by (or in the) faith of thy soul; for why this is the keeping of (the) command-ments.
ECCLESIASTICUS 32:24  He that believeth to (or in) God, taketh heed to the commandments; and he that trusteth in him, shall not be made less, either deceived.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:1  Evils shall not come to him that dreadeth God; but God shall keep (or shall guard) him in temptation, and shall deliver [him] from evils.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:2  A wise man hateth not the commandments, and rightfulnesses [or rightwisenesses]; and he shall not be hurtled down, as in the tempest of a ship (or as a ship in a tempest).
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:3  A wise man believeth in the law of God, and the law is faithful to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:4  He that maketh open asking, shall make ready [or shall prepare] a word; and so he shall pray, and shall be heard, and he shall keep (the) teach-ing, and then he shall answer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:5  The entrails of a fool be as a wheel of a cart, and his thoughts as an axle able to turn about.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:6  An horse a stallion, so and a friend a scorner, neigheth under each (one) sitting above.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:7  Why a day overcometh a day, and again the light overcometh light, and a year overcometh a year, (and) the sun overcometh the sun?
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:8  Those be parted of (or separated by) the cunning (or the knowing) of the Lord, by the sun made, and keeping the commandment of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:9  And it [or he] shall change [the] times and the feast days of them, and in those times the Jews hallowed holy days, or holidays, at an hour. God enhanced and magnified of those holy days or holidays; and of those he setted [or put] into the number of days;
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:10  and God made all men of firm earth, and of nesh earth [or soil], whereof Adam was formed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:11  In the multitude of (the) cunning (or the knowing) of the Lord, he parted them, and changed the ways of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:12  (Some) Of them God blessed, and enhanced (or exalted); and (some) of them he hallowed, and chose to (or for) himself [or presented]; (some) of them he cursed, and made low, and turned them from the departing [or to the severing] of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:13  As (the) clay of a potter is in the hand of him, to make [or to form] and dispose, (so) that all the ways thereof be after the ordinance of him [or after his disposition]; so a man is in the hand of him that made him; and he shall yield to him by [or after] his doom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:14  Against evil is good, and against life is death; so and a sinner is against a just man [or the rightwise].
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:15  And so behold thou into all the works of the Highest; two things against twain, and one thing against one [or two against two, one against one].
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:16  And I the last waked, and as he that gathereth dregs of grapes, after the gatherers of grapes. And I hoped in the blessing of God; and as he that gathereth grapes, I filled the presser.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:17  Behold ye, for I travailed not to (or for) me alone, but to [or for] all that seek cunning, (or knowing, or knowledge).
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:18  Great men, and all peoples hear ye me; and ye governors of the church, perceive with ears.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:19  Give thou not power over thee in thy life to a son, and to a woman [or a wife], to a brother, and to a friend; and give thou not thy possession to another man, lest peradventure it repent thee, and thou beseech for those (again).
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:20  While thou art alive, [or livest], and breathest yet, each man shall not change thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:21  For it is better, that thy sons pray thee, than that thou behold into the hands of thy sons.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:22  In all thy works be thou sove-reign; give thou not a wem into thy glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:23  In the day of (the) ending of (the) days of thy life, and in the time of thy going out [or thy death], part [or deal (out)] thine heritage.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:24  Meats, and a rod, and a burden to an ass; bread, and chastising [or disci-pline], and work to (or for) a servant.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:25  He worketh in, or under, chastis-ing, and seeketh to have rest; slake or slack thou (thine) hands to him, and he seeketh freedom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:26  A yoke and bridle bow down an hard neck; and busy workings bow down a servant. Torment and stocks to (or for) an evil-willed servant;
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:27  send thou him into working, lest he be idle; for why idleness hath taught much malice.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:28  Ordain thou [or set] him in work, for so it becometh him; (so) that if he obeyeth not, bow thou down him in stocks,
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:29  and make thou not him large over any man, that is, give thou not to him power over any man, but without doom, do thou nothing grievous [or heavy].
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:30  If a faithful servant is to thee, be he as thy soul [or thy life] to thee; treat thou him so as a brother, for thou hast bought him in (or with) the blood of life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 33:31  If thou hurtest him unjustly, he shall be turned into fleeing away [or into flight]; and if he enhancing goeth away, thou knowest not whom thou shalt seek, and in what way thou shalt seek him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:1  Vain hope and a leasing (or a lie), to an unwise man; and dreams [or swevens] enhance unprudent men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:2  As he that taketh [or catcheth (at)] a shadow, and pursueth wind, so and he that taketh heed to leasings seen, [or to the seen leasings], or in vain dreams.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:3  After this thing is the sight of dreams [or swevens]; before the face of a man is the likeness of another man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:4  What shall be cleansed of him that is unclean [or Of the unclean, what shall be cleansed], and what true thing shall be said of a liar?
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:5  False divining of error, and false divinings by chittering (or chattering) of birds, and dreams of witches, (all) is vanity. And as the heart of a woman travailing of [or bearing (a)] child, thine heart suffereth fantasies;
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:6  no but visitation is sent out of (or from) the Highest, give thou not thine heart in (or to) those dreams.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:7  For why dreams have made many men for to err, and men hoping in those fell down. [Many men forsooth swevens made to err, and (they) fell away hoping in them.]
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:8  The word of the law of God and of his prophets, shall be made perfect without leasing (or without lies); and wisdom in the mouth of a faithful man shall be made plain.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:9  What knoweth he, that is not assayed? A man assayed in many things, shall think many things; and he that learned many things, shall tell out understanding.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:10  He that is not assayed [or not expert (or experienced)], knoweth few things; forsooth he that is a fool in many things, shall multiply malice.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:11  What manner things know he, that is not assayed? He that is not planted, that is, hath not set root of (or in) understanding, and desire in (or for) good, shall be plenteous in wickedness [or shall abound (in) shrewdness (or in depravity)]. I saw many things in telling out, and full many customs of words.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:12  Sometime I was in peril unto death, for the cause of these things; and I was delivered by the grace of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:13  The spirit of them that dread God is sought, and shall be blessed in the beholding of him. For why the hope of them is into God saving them; and the eyes of the Lord be into (or upon) them, that love him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:14  He that dreadeth God, shall not tremble [or quake] for anything, and he shall not dread; for why God is his hope.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:15  The soul of him that dreadeth the Lord, is blessed. To whom beholdeth he, and who is his strength?
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:16  The eyes of the Lord be on them that dread him. God is a defender of might, steadfastness [or firmament] of virtue, covering of (or from) heat, and a shadowing place of (or at) midday; beseeching of offending, that is, hearing beseeching for offenses, and help of (or from) falling,
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:17  enhancing the soul, and lighten-ing the eyes, and giving health, and life, and blessing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:18  The offering of him that offereth of wicked thing, that is, of thing gotten unjustly, is defouled; and the scornings of unjust men be not well pleasant [or well-pleasing].
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:19  The Lord alone is to them that abide him in the way of truth, and of rightfulness [or of rightwiseness]. The Highest approveth not (of) the gifts of wicked men, neither beholdeth in (or on) the offerings of wicked men, neither in (or for) the multitude of their sacrifices he shall do [or shall have] mercy to (or for their) sins.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:20  He that offereth sacrifice of the chattel [or substance] of poor men, is as he that slayeth the son in the sight of his father.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:21  The bread of needy men is the life of a poor man; he that defraudeth him, is a man of blood.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:22  He that taketh away bread (earn-ed) in (or with) sweat, is as he that slayeth his neighbour. He that shed-deth out blood, and he that doeth fraud to an hired man, be brethren.
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:23  One building, and one destroy-ing; what profiteth it to them, no but travail?
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:24  One praying, and one cursing; whose voice shall the Lord hear?
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:25  What profiteth the washing of him, that is washed for a dead body, and toucheth again a dead body?
ECCLESIASTICUS 34:26  So a man that fasteth in his sins, and again doing the same sins, what profiteth he in meeking himself? who shall hear his prayer?
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:1  He that keepeth the word of God, multiplieth prayer. Wholeful [or Wholesome] sacrifice is to take heed to (or of) the commandments, and to depart [or go away] from all wicked-ness. And to offer the pleasing of sacrifice for unrightfulnesses [or (for) unrightwisenesses], and beseeching for sins, is to go away from unrightful-ness [or unrightwiseness].
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:2  He that offereth purest flour of wheat, shall yield grace, that is, shall give a pleasant (or a pleasing) service to God; and he that doeth mercy, offereth a sacrifice.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:3  It is well pleasant [or well-pleas-ing] to the Lord, to go away from wickedness; and prayer is to go away from unrightfulness [or unrightwise-ness].
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:4  Thou shalt not appear void (or empty) before the sight of God;
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:5  for why all these things be done for the behests, (or for the commands, or the commandments) of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:6  The offering of a just man [or of the rightwise] maketh fat the altar, and is (the) odour of sweetness in the sight of the Highest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:7  The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable, and the Lord shall not for-get the mind (or the memory) of him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:8  With good will yield thou glory to God, and make thou not less the first fruits of thine hands.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:9  In each gift [or In all gifts] make glad thy cheer, and in full out joying hallow thy tithes.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:10  Give thou to the Highest after his [free] gift, that is, after the quantity of thy goods, which thou hast of (or from) God; and with good eye make thou the findings of thine hands, that is, with rightful intent, ordain thy good works, to the praising of God and not of man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:11  For why the Lord is a yielder, and he shall yield sevenfold so much [or as much] to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:12  Do not thou offer shrewd (or de-praved) gifts; for he shall not receive those [or them]. And do not thou behold an unjust [or the unrightwise] sacrifice; for the Lord is judge, and glory, or taking, (or favouring) of person(s) is not at [or with] him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:13  The Lord shall not take a person against a poor man (or The Lord will not favour some person over a poor person); and he shall hear the prayer of him that is hurt.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:14  He shall not despise the prayers of a fatherless child, neither a widow, if she sheddeth [or poured] out (the) speech of wailing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:15  Whether the tears of a widow go not down to the cheek, and the crying of her on him that leadeth forth those tears? For why those ascend from the cheek unto heaven, and the Lord hearing shall not delight in those [or in them].
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:16  He that worshippeth God in delighting, shall be received; and his prayer shall nigh unto the clouds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:17  The prayer of him that meeketh himself shall pierce (the) clouds, and till it nigheth (or approacheth), he shall not be comforted, and he shall not go away, till the Highest behold (him). And the Lord shall not be far [or long away], but he shall judge just [or rightwise] men, and shall make doom;
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:18  and the Strongest shall not have patience in those [or (towards) them], that (or till) he trouble the back(s) of them. And he shall yield vengeance to (the) folks [or (the) Gentiles], till he take away the fullness [or the plenty] of proud men, and trouble (al)to-gether the sceptres of wicked men;
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:19  till he yield to men after their deeds, and after the works of Adam , and after the presumption of him; till he deem the doom of his people, and shall delight just [or rightwise] men in his mercy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 35:20  The mercy of God is fair in the time of tribulation, as clouds of rain in the time of dryness [or of drought].
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:1  God of all things, have thou mercy on us; and behold thou us, and show to us the light of thy merciful doings.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:2  And send thy dread on heathen men, that sought not thee, (so) that they know that no God is, no but thou; that they tell out thy great [worthy] deeds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:3  Raise [up] thine hand on heathen men aliens, (so) that they see thy power.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:4  For as thou were hallowed in us in the sight of them, so in our sight thou shalt be magnified in them;
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:5  (so) that they know thee, as and we have known (thee), that none other is God, except thee, Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:6  Make thou new signs, and change thou marvels; glorify the hand, and the right arm.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:7  Raise [up] thou strong vengeance, and shed out ire [or pour out wrath]; take away the adversary, and torment the enemy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:8  Haste thou the time, and have thou mind on the end, (so) that they tell out thy marvels.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:9  And he that is saved, be devour-ed in the ire of flame; and they that treat worst thy people, find perdition.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:10  All-break thou the head(s) of princes, and of enemies, saying, None other is [or There is none other], except us.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:11  Gather thou together all the lineages of Jacob, and know they that no God is, no but thou [or there is no God but thou], (so) that they tell out thy great deeds; and thou shalt inherit them, as at the beginning.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:12  Have thou mercy on thy people, on which thy name is called in to help; and on Israel, whom thou madest even to thy first engendered [or (be)gotten] son.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:13  Have thou mercy on Jerusalem, the city of thine hallowing, on the city of thy rest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:14  [Full]-fill thou Zion with thy virtues, that may not be told out [or untellable], and fill thy people with thy glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:15  Give thou witnessing, that at [or from] the beginning they were thy creatures; and raise thou (the) prayers, which the former prophets spake in thy name.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:16  Lord, give thou meed (or reward) to them that abide thee, (so) that thy prophets be found true [or faithful];
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:17  and hear thou the prayer of thy servants. After the blessing of Aaron give thou to thy people, and (ad)dress (or direct) thou us into the way of rightfulness; (so) that all men know, that dwell in (or on the) earth, that thou art God, the beholder of worlds.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:18  The womb shall eat all meat(s), and one meat is better than another meat.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:19  Cheeks touch meat almost, and an unwise heart receiveth false [or leasing (or lying)] words.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:20  A shrewd (or depraved) heart shall give heaviness, and a wise man shall against-stand [or withstand] it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:21  A woman shall take each knave [or male] child, and (or but) a daughter is [or there is a daughter] better than a son.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:22  The fairness of a woman maketh glad the face of her husband, and (so) she shall bring desire (for herself) over all the covetousness [or (the) lust] of (her) man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:23  If there is a tongue of healing, [or of curing, (or of caring)], there is also (one) of assuaging, and of mercy; (and) the husband of her is not after (or like most of) the (other) sons of men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:24  He that hath in possession a good woman, beginneth (a) possession; she is an help like (to) him(self), and a pillar as (or of) rest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:25  Where an hedge is not, the possession shall be ravished (or snatched) away [or broken]; and where a woman is not, a needy man waileth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 36:26  To whom believeth he that hath no nest, and boweth down wherever it is dark, as a thief girt [or girded up], skipping out from city into city?
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:1  Each friend shall say, And I have coupled friendship; but that [or there] is a friend, a friend by name alone.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:2  Whether sorrow is not till to death? Forsooth a fellow of (the) table and a friend shall be turned to enmity.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:3  A! the worst [or O! most shrewd (or depraved)] presumption, whereof art thou made to cover dry malice, and the guilefulness thereof [or the treachery of it]?
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:4  A fellow of (the) table shall be merry with a friend in delightings, and in the day of tribulation he shall be (an) adversary.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:5  A fellow of (the) table shall have sorrow with a friend, for cause [or because] of the womb (or the belly); and he shall take (up a) shield against an enemy.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:6  Forget thou not thy friend in thy soul, and be thou not unmindful of him in thy works. Do not thou take counsel with the father of thy wife; and hide thou counsel from them that have envy to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:7  Each counsellor showeth counsel, but there is a counsellor to, [or in], (or only for) himself.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:8  Keep thy soul from an evil counsellor; first know thou, what is his need, and what he shall think in his soul; lest peradventure he send a stake, [or he put a pole, or a pale] into the earth,
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:9  and say to thee, Thy way is good, and (then) he stand again-ward, to see what shall befall to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:10  With an unreligious man, treat thou (not) of (or about) holiness, and with an unjust [or unrightwise] man, (not) of (or about) rightfulness [or rightwiseness] ,
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:11  and with a woman, (not) of (or about) these things which she hateth [or envieth]. With a fearedful man, treat thou (not) of (or about) battle, with a merchant, (not) of (or about) carrying over of merchandises to chapping[or (about)(ex)changing]; with a buyer, (not) of (or about) selling, with an envious man, (not) of (or about) graces to be done; with an unpiteous man, (not) of (or about) pity, with an unhonest man, (not) of (or about) honesty, with a workman of the field [or the field worker], (not) of (or about) each work; with a work-man hired by the year [or the annual worker], (not) of (or about) the ending of the year, with a slow servant, (not) of (or about) much working. Give thou not attention [or Take thou not heed] to these men in all counsel,
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:12  but be thou busy with an holy man, whomever thou knowest (is) keeping God’s dread, whose soul is after thy soul. Whoever doubteth in darknesses, shall not have sorrow with thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:13  And establish thou the heart of good counsel with thee; for why another thing is not more than it (is) to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:14  The soul of an holy man telleth out truths sometime; more than seven beholders [or lookers about], sitting on high for to behold.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:15  And in all these things beseech thou the Highest, that he (ad)dress (or direct) thy way in truth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:16  Before all works a soothfast (or a true) word go before thee; and a stead-fast counsel go before each deed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:17  A wicked, [or shrewd, (or de-praved)] word shall change the heart,
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:18  of which heart four parts come forth; good and evil, life and death; and a busy tongue is lord of those.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:19  A wise man hath taught many men, and (or but) he is (not) sweet to his (own) soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:20  He that speaketh sophistically, either by sophism, is hateful; he shall be defrauded in each thing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:21  For why grace is not given of (or from) the Lord to him, for he is defrauded of all wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:22  A wise man is wise to his (own) soul, and the fruits of his wit be worthy to be praised.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:23  A wise man teacheth his people, and the fruits of his wit be faithful.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:24  A wise man shall be filled with blessings, and they that see him shall praise him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:25  The life of a man is in the number of days; but the days of Israel be unnumberable.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:26  A wise man in the people shall inherit honour, and his name shall be living without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:27  Son, assay thy soul in thy life; and if it is wicked, give thou not power to it;
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:28  for why not all things speed to (or be expedient for) all men, and not each kind pleaseth each soul.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:29  Do not thou be greedy in each eating, and shed thou not out thee [or pour thee not out] [up] on each meat.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:30  For in many meats shall be sickness, and greediness shall nigh unto choler.
ECCLESIASTICUS 37:31  Many men died for (or from) gluttony; but he that is abstinent, shall increase [or add (to)](his) life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:1  Honour thou a leech (or Honour a physician), for need; for why the Highest hath made [or formed] him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:2  For why all medicine is of (or from) God; and he shall take of (or receive from) the king a gift.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:3  The cunning of a leech shall enhance his head (or The knowledge of a physician shall exalt or lift up his head); and he shall be praised in the sight of great men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:4  The Highest hath made [or (hath) formed](out) of the earth medicine; and a prudent man shall not loathe it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:5  Whether bitter water was not made sweet of (or by) a tree? The virtue of those things came by experience to the knowing of men;
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:6  and the Highest gave cunning (or knowing) to men, for to be honoured in his marvels.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:7  A man healing [or curing] in (or with) these things, shall assuage sorrow,
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:8  and an ointment-maker shall make pigments of sweetness, and shall make anointings of health; and his works shall not be ended. For why the peace of God is on the face of (the) earth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:9  My son, despise not thyself in thy sickness; but pray thou (to) the Lord, and he shall heal [or cure] thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:10  Turn thou away from sin, and (ad)dress (or direct) thine hands, and cleanse thine heart from all sin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:11  Give thou sweetness, and the mind (or a memorial) of clean [or tried] flour of wheat, and make thou (a) fat offering;
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:12  and give thou place to a leech (or to a physician). For the Lord made him, and depart he not [or go he not away] from thee; for his works be needful to thee.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:13  For why (a) time is (or shall be), when thou shalt fall into the hands of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:14  Forsooth they shall beseech the Lord, that he (ad)dress (or direct) the work of them, and health for their living.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:15  He that trespasseth in the sight of him, that made him, shall fall into the hands of the leech (or the physician).
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:16  Son, bring thou forth tears on, (or over, or for) a dead man, and thou as suffering hard things begin to weep; and by [or after] doom, (or according to custom), cover thou the body of him, and despise thou not his bury-ing.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:17  But for backbiting, bear thou bitterly the mourning of him (for) one day; and be thou comforted for sorrow [or take comfort for heavi-ness]. And make thou mourning after his merit [or deserving](for) one day, either twain [or two], for backbiting.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:18  For why death hast(en)eth of (or from) sorrow, and covereth virtue (or strength); and the sorrow of heart boweth the head.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:19  Sorrow dwelleth in leading away; and the chattel [or the substance] of a needy man is after his heart.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:20  Give thou not thine heart in sorrow, but put it away from thee; and have thou mind on the last things,
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:21  and do not thou forget. For why no (re)turning is from death to this present life, and thou shalt nothing profit to this dead man[or] and to this thou shalt nothing profit; and thou shalt harm worst thyself.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:22  Be thou mindful of my doom (or Remember my judgement); for also thine shall be thus, to me yesterday, and to thee today.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:23  In the rest of a dead man, make thou his mind (or his memory) to have rest; and comfort thou him, in the going out of his spirit.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:24  Write thou wisdom in the time of voidness; and he that is made less in (doing) deeds, shall perceive wisdom; for he shall be filled of [or with] wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:25  He that holdeth the plow (or the plough), and he that hath glory in a goad, driveth oxes [or oxen] with a prick, and he liveth in the works of those [or them]; and his telling is in the sons of bulls.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:26  He shall give his heart to turn furrows; and his waking shall be about the fatness of (the) kine.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:27  So each carpenter, and principal workman, that passeth the night as the day; that engraveth images en-graved [or the which graved graven brooches], and the busyness of him diverseth [or varieth] the painture; he shall give his heart [in] to the likeness of painture (or of painting), and by his waking he performeth the work.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:28  So a smith sitting beside the anfelt (or the anvil), and beholding the work of iron, the heat of fire burneth his fleshes; and he striveth in the heat of the furnace. The voice of a hammer maketh new his ear; and his eye is against (or towards) the like-ness of a vessel. He shall give his heart into the performing of (the) works; and by his waking he shall adorn unperfection, that is, matter (or material) which he bringeth to perfection of form.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:29  So a potter sitting at his work, turning a wheel with his feet, which is put ever[more] in busyness for his work; and all his working is unnumberable.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:30  In his arm he shall form (the) clay; and before his feet he shall bow (down) his virtue (or strength). He shall give his heart to end perfectly something; and by his waking he shall cleanse the furnace.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:31  All these men hoped in their hands; and each man is wise in his craft.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:32  A city is not builded without all these men. And they shall not dwell [in], neither go [in];
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:33  and they shall not skip over into the church. They shall not sit on the seat of a judge; and they shall not understand the testament of doom, neither they shall make open teach-ing and doom; and they shall not be found in parables.
ECCLESIASTICUS 38:34  But they shall confirm the creature (or the nature) of the world, and their prayer is the working of craft;
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:1  and they give their soul, and they ask together [or together seeking] in the law of the Highest. A wise man shall seek out the wisdom of all (the) eld [or old] men; and he shall give attention in (or to the) prophets.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:2  He shall keep the telling(s) of (the) named men; and he shall enter (al)together into the hard sentences [or the slynesses] of parables.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:3  He shall seek out the privy things of proverbs; and he shall be conver-sant in the hid things of parables.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:4  He shall minister in the midst of great men; and he shall appear in the sight of the chief judge. He shall pass into the land of alien folks; for he shall assay goods, and evils in all things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:5  He shall give his heart to wake early to the Lord that made him; and he shall beseech in the sight of the Highest. He shall open his mouth in prayer; and he shall beseech for his trespasses.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:6  For if the great Lord will (or desire to), he shall fill him with the spirit of understanding. And he shall send the words of his wisdom, as rains; and in prayer he shall acknowl-edge to the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:7  And he, that is, the Lord, shall (ad)dress (or direct) his counsel, and teaching; and shall counsel in his hid things.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:8  He shall make open the wisdom of his teaching; and he shall have glory in the law of the testament of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:9  Many men shall praise his wisdom; and it shall not be done away till into the world. His mind shall not go away [or The memory of him shall not go away]; and his name shall be sought from generation into generation.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:10  Folks shall tell out his wisdom; and the church shall tell [out] his praising.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:11  If his name dwelleth, he shall leave more than a thousand; and if he resteth, it shall profit to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:12  Yet I shall take counsel to tell out, for I am [full]-filled as with madness; and mine inner spirit saith in voice,
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:13  Ye fruits of God, hear me, and make ye fruit, as roses planted on (or by) the rivers of waters.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:14  Have ye odour of sweetness, as the Lebanon hath. Bring forth flowers, as a lily; give ye odour, and make ye boughs into grace. And praise ye together a song; and bless ye the Lord in his works.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:15  Give ye great honour to his name, and acknowledge ye to him in the voice of your lips, in songs of lips, and in harps; and thus ye shall say in acknowledging,
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:16  All the works of the Lord be full good.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:17  Forsooth water as an heap of stones stood at his word; and as receptacles of waters in the word of his mouth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:18  For why peaceableness is made in his commandment; and no default [or less(en)ing] is in the health of him, that is, in (the) saving made by him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:19  The works of each [or all] flesh be before him; and nothing is hid from his eyes.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:20  He beholdeth from the world till into the world; and nothing is won-derful [or is marvellous] in his sight.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:21  It is not to say, What is this thing, either, What is that thing? for why all things shall be sought in their time.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:22  The blessing of him shall flow as a flood;
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:23  and as the great flood filled greatly the earth, so his ire [or wrath] shall inherit in folks, that sought not him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:24  As he turned waters into dryness-es [or into drought], and the earth was dried, and his ways were (ad)dressed (or directed) to the ways of them; so offensions (or stumbling blocks) in his ire [or in (his) wrath]be (ad) dressed (or directed) to sinners.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:25  Good things were made at the beginning to (or for) good men; so good things and evil be made to (or for) worst men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:26  The beginning of needful [or necessary] thing(s) to the life of men, (be) water, fire, and iron, and salt, and milk, and bread of clean [or tried] flour of wheat, and honey, and a cluster of grape(s), and oil, and cloth(es)[or clothing].
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:27  All these things shall turn to holy men into goods; so and to unfaithful [or unpious] men and to sinners into evils.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:28  Spirits be that be made [or formed] to (or for) vengeance; and in their madness they confirmed their torments. And in the time of ending they shall shed [or pour] out virtue; and they shall confound (or confuse) the strong vengeance of him that made them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:29  Fire, hail, hunger, and death; all these things be made [or be formed] to (or for) vengeance;
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:30  the teeth of beasts, and scorpions, and serpents, and a sword punishing wicked men into destroying.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:31  In the commandments of him, those [or they] shall eat, and those [or they] shall be made ready on the earth in need; and in their times those [or they] shall not (over)-pass one word.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:32  Therefore from the beginning I was confirmed (or certain); and I counselled, and thought, and left (it all) written (down).
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:33  All the works of the Lord be good; and each work shall serve in his (or its) hour.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:34  It is not to say, This is worse than that; for why all things shall be (ap)proved in their time.
ECCLESIASTICUS 39:35  And now in all the heart and mouth praise ye together, and bless ye the name of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:1  Great occupation is made to all men, and an heavy yoke on the sons of Adam, from the day of the going out of the womb of their mother, till into the day of burying into the mother of all men, that is, into the earth.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:2  The thoughts of them, and the dreads of (the) heart, (the) findings of abiding, and the day of ending;
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:3  from him that sitteth before on a glorious seat (or a throne of glory), unto a man made low into earth and ashes;
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:4  from him that useth jacinth, (or hyacinth), [or blue silk], and beareth a crown, unto him that is covered with raw linen cloth (or a linen cloak),
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:5  madness (or anger), envy, noise, doubting, and dread of death, wrath-fulness dwelling continually, and strife; and in the time of resting [or repast] in the bed, the sleep of night changeth his cunning (or his know-ing, or his knowledge).
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:6  Forsooth a little is as nought in rest; beholding is of him in sleep as in the day. He is disturbed (or is troubled) in the sight of his heart, as he that escapeth [or escaped] in the day of battle.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:7  He rose up in the day of his health, (or his deliverance), and dread-ing not at any dread,
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:8  with all flesh, from man unto beast, and sevenfold (more), that is, grievous punishment, shall come on sinners.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:9  At these things, death, blood, striving [or strife], and sword, oppressings, hunger, and sorrow, and beatings;
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:10  all these things be made on wicked men, and the great flood was made for them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:11  For why all (the) things that be of the earth, shall (re)turn into the earth; and all (the things that be of the) waters shall (re)turn into the sea.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:12  All gift, given for (the) destroying of rightfulness, and wickedness, done for gift, shall be done away; and faith shall stand into the world (for ever-more).
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:13  The riches [or The substances] of unjust men shall be made dry [or dried (up)] as a flood; and shall sound as a great thunder in (the) rain.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:14  An unjust man shall be glad in opening his hands; so trespassers [or law-breakers] shall fail in the end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:15  The sons of (the) sons of wicked [or unpious] men shall not multiply branches; and (be like) unclean roots sown on the cop (or the top) of a stone.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:16  Greenness beside each water; and at the brink of the flood (or bank of the river), it shall be drawn out by the root before all (the) hay.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:17  Grace as paradise in blessings; and mercy dwelleth into the world.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:18  The life of a workman sufficient to himself shall be made sweet; and thou shalt find treasure therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:19  (The) Building of a city shall con-firm a name; and a woman without wem [or undefouled] shall be reckon-ed above [or over] this, for why her steadfastness shall stand without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:20  Wine and music make glad the heart; and (or but the) love of wisdom gladdeth above [or over] ever either.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:21  Pipes and psaltery make sweet melody; and (or but) a sweet tongue (is) above [or over] ever either.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:22  An eye shall desire grace and fair-ness; and green sowings above these things [or over these green tilthes].
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:23  A friend and [a meat]-fellow coming together in time; and (or but) a woman with a man (is) above [or over] ever either.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:24  Brethren into help in the time of tribulation comfort much; and (or but) mercy shall deliver more than they [or over them].
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:25  Gold and silver, and setting of feet; and (or but) counsel well-pleas-ing is above [or over] ever either.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:26  Riches and virtues enhance the heart; and (or but) the dread of the Lord (is) more than this. Making less [or less(en)ing] is not in the dread of the Lord; and in that dread it is not to seek help.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:27  The dread of the Lord is as (a) paradise of blessing; and the blessings of God covered him above all glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:28  Son, in the time of thy life, be thou not needy, that is, in (the) time of (thy) present life, granted to thee to work well, be thou not idle; for it is better to die, then to be needy, that is, it is better to die bodily, then to be idle, by which a man dieth ghostly (or spiritually).
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:29  A man beholding into another man’s board, his life is not in the thought of lifelode (or about liveli-hood); for he sustaineth his life with other men’s meats. Forsooth a chas-tised man and learned [or disciplined and taught], shall keep himself.
ECCLESIASTICUS 40:30  Neediness shall be defouled [or made] in the mouth of an unprudent, or (a) slow and idle, man; and (or but) fire shall burn in his womb.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:1  A! [or O!] death, thy mind is full bitter to an unjust [or an unrightwise] man, and having peace in his riches; to a restful [or quiet] man, and whose ways be (ad)dressed (or directed) in all things, that is, hath prosperity in all temporal things, and yet mighty to take meat.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:2  A! [or O!] death, thy doom (or thy judgement) is good to a needy man, and which is made less in strengths, and faileth for age, and to whom is care of all things, and unbelieveful, that loseth (or destroyeth) wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:3  Do not thou dread the doom of death, that is, set thou thee in such a state, (so) that the doom of death be good to (or for) thee; have thou mind what things were before thee, and what things shall come on (or after) thee; this doom is of the Lord to each man.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:4  And those things that shall come on (or after) thee in the good pleasance (or through the good pleasure) of the Highest; whether ten years, either an hundred, either a thousand. For why none accusing (or excusing) of life is in hell (or in the grave), that is, no man may excuse him (self) there, in alleging (the) goodness of (his) life.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:5  The sons of abominations be the sons of sinners; and they that dwell beside the houses of wicked men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:6  The heritage of the sons of sinners shall perish; and the continuance of shame [or reproof] with the seed of them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:7  (The) Sons (will)(com)plain of a wicked father; for they be in shame [or in reproof] for him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:8  Woe to you, ye wicked men, that have forsaken the law of the Highest.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:9  And if ye be born, ye shall be born in cursedness; and if ye be dead, your part shall be in cursedness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:10  All things that be of the earth, shall (re)turn into the earth; so wicked men shall turn from cursing into perdition.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:11  The mourning of men is in (or for) the body of them; but the name of wicked men shall be done away.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:12  Have thou busyness of (or for) a good name; for why this shall dwell more with thee, than a thousand treasures great and precious.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:13  The number of days is the term of (a) good life; but a good name shall dwell without end.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:14  Sons, keep ye teaching in peace; for why wisdom hid, and treasure unseen, what profit is in ever either?
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:15  Better is a man that hideth his folly, than a man that hideth his wisdom.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:16  Nevertheless (re)turn ye again in these things that come forth of (or from)[or go out of] my mouth. For it is not good to keep all unreverence, and not all things please all men in faith.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:17  Be ye ashamed of fornication, before father, and before mother; and of a leasing (or of a lie), before a justice, and before a mighty man;
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:18  and of trespass, before a prince, and before a judge; and of wicked-ness, before a synagogue, and a people; and of unrightfulness, or unrightwiseness, before a fellow, and a friend;
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:19  and of theft, in the place wherein thou dwellest; of the truth and the testament of God; of sitting [down] at the meat in loaves; and of the blem-ishing [or darkening] of [the] gift (or of giving), and (of) taking [of (the) taken];
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:20  of stillness, before them that greet [or saluting](thee); of the beholding of a lecherous woman; and of the turning away of the cheer (or the face) of a cousin.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:21  Turn thou not away thy face from thy neighbour; and be thou ware of taking away a part, and not restoring (it). Behold thou not the woman of another man;
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:22  and ensearch thou not her hand-maid, neither stand thou at her bed. Be thou ware of friends, of the words of upbraiding [or of reproof]; and when thou hast given, upbraid thou not.
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:23  Double thou not a word of hearing, (and) of the showing of an hid word;
ECCLESIASTICUS 41:24  and thou shalt be verily (or truly) without shame [or confusion], and thou shalt find grace in the sight of all men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:1  Be thou not (a)shamed for all these things; and take [or accept] thou not a person, (so) that thou do trespass.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:2  Be thou ware of the law and testament of the Highest, of doom to justify a wicked man; [of the law of the Highest, and of the testament of doom, to justify the unpious;]
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:3  of the word of fellows, and of way-goers, and of the giving of (the) heritage of friends;
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:4  of the evenness of balance, and of weights, of the getting of many things, and of few things;
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:5  of (the) corruption of buying, and of merchants, and of much chastising [or much discipline] of sons; and of a worst servant, to make the side to bleed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:6  A sealing, either closing, is good on a wicked woman. Where be many hands, close thou (up);
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:7  and whatever thing thou shalt betake (or receive), number thou, and weigh thou; forsooth describe thou, either write (down), each gift, and taking (or receiving in).
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:8  Abstain thou from the teaching of an unwitty (or unwise) man, and fool, and of elder men that be deemed of (or by the) young men; and thou shalt be learned in all things, and thou shalt be commendable [or (ap)prov-able (or approved)] in the sight of all men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:9  An hid daughter of a father is waking [or watch(ing)] and busyness of (or for) him; she shall take away sleep; lest peradventure she be made (an) adulteress in her young waxing age, and lest she dwelling with the husband, be made hateful;
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:10  lest anytime she be defouled in her virginity [or be polluted in her maidenhood], and be found with child in the keeping of her father; lest peradventure she dwelling with the husband, do trespass, either certainly be made barren.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:11  Ordain thou keeping [or ward] on a lecherous daughter, lest any time she make thee to come into shame [or reproof] to [thine] enemies, of backbiting in the city, and of casting out of the people; and she make thee ashamed in the multitude of people.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:12  Do not thou take heed to each man (or to each person) in the fair-ness, that is, in delighting in the beholding of his (or their) fairness; and do not thou dwell in the midst of women.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:13  For why a moth cometh forth of (or from) clothes, and (the) wicked-ness of a man cometh forth of (or from) a woman.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:14  For why the wickedness of a man is better, that is, less evil, than a woman doing well, and a woman shaming into shame (or reproach) .
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:15  Therefore be thou mindful of the works of the Lord; and I shall tell (out) the works of the Lord, which I saw, in the words of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 42:16  The sun lightening [or shining through] beheld by all things; and the work thereof is full of the glory of the Lord.

He had not mind on [or remembered not] their sins, neither gave them to their enemies; but he purged them in (or by) the hand of Isaiah, the holy prophet, by Isaiah praying for them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 48:21  The angel of the Lord casted down the castles (or the hosts) of (the) Assyrians, and all-brake them.
ECCLESIASTICUS 48:22  For why Hezekiah did that that pleased the Lord, and went strongly in the way of David, his father; which way Isaiah, the great prophet, and faithful in the sight of God, commanded to him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 48:23  In the days of him the sun went again aback; and God increased life to the king.

ECCLESIASTICUS 49:1  The mind (or the memory) of Josiah made in the making of odour, is (like) the work of a pigment-maker. In each mouth his mind (or his memory) shall be made (as) sweet as honey, and as music [or as melody] in the feast of wine.
ECCLESIASTICUS 49:2  He was (ad)dressed (or directed) of (or by) God in the penance of (the) folk, for he brought the people of his realm to penance for their sins, and to the worshipping of (the) very (or the true) God, and destroyed idolatry; and he took away the abominations of wickedness.
ECCLESIASTICUS 49:3  And the heart of him governed (un)to the Lord [or And he governed (un)to the Lord his heart]; and in the days of sins he strengthened piety.
ECCLESIASTICUS 49:4  Except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all [the] kings did sin. For why the kings of Judah left the law of (the) mighty God, and despised the dread of God.
ECCLESIASTICUS 49:5  For they gave their realm to other men, and their glory to an alien folk.

ECCLESIASTICUS 49:10  And the bones of (the) twelve prophets appear [or spring out] from their place; and they strengthened Jacob, and again-bought (or redeem-ed) them in (or by) the faith of their virtue.

ECCLESIASTICUS 49:12  and Jesus (or Joshua), the son of Jehozadak? which in their days build-ed an house [or the house], and enhanced the holy temple to the Lord, made ready into everlasting glory.
ECCLESIASTICUS 49:13  And Nehemiah in the mind of much time, that raised [up] to (or for) us the walls, that were cast down, and made the gates and (the) locks to stand; which Nehemiah raised [up] our houses.

ECCLESIASTICUS 51:1  Lord King, I shall acknowledge to thee; and I shall (al)together praise thee, my Saviour. I shall acknowledge to thy name,
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:2  for thou art made an helper and defender to me; and thou hast delivered my body from perdition, from the snare of a wicked tongue, and from the lips of them that work a leasing (or a lie); and in the sight of them that stand nigh, thou art made an helper to me.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:3  And thou hast delivered me, by [or after] the multitude of mercy of thy name, from roarers made ready to (or for) meat; from the hands of them that sought my soul, and from many tribulations that (en)compassed me;
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:4  from (the) over-laying of flame that compassed me, and in the midst of (the) fire I was not burnt;
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:5  from the depth of the womb of hell, and from a tongue defouled, and from a word of leasing (or from lying words);
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:6  from a wicked king, and from a tongue unjust [or an unrightwise tongue]. Unto the death, my soul shall praise thee, Lord; and my life was nighing in (or to) hell (or the grave) beneath.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:7  They compassed me on each side, and none was that helped (me); I was beholding into (or looking for) the help of men, and none was.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:8  Lord, I had mind on thy mercy, and on thy working (al)together, that be from the world; for thou deliverest them that abide thee, and thou deliverest them from the hand(s) of heathen men.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:9  Thou enhancedest my dwelling on (the) earth; and I besought for death floating [or flowing] down.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:10  I called to help the Lord, (the) father (or the Father) of my Lord, that he forsake not me in the day of my tribulation, and forsake not me with-out help, in the time of them that be proud.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:11  I shall praise thy name continual-ly, and I shall praise it (al)together in acknowledging [or in confession]; and my prayer is heard.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:12  And thou hast delivered me from perdition, and thou hast delivered me from the wicked time. Therefore I shall acknowledge, and I shall say praising to thee; and I shall bless the name of the Lord.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:13  When yet I was younger, before that I erred, or that I wandered, (or before that I travelled abroad), I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:14  Before the time of eld (age), I asked for it, and unto the last things, I shall inquire (for) it [or I shall greatly seek it];
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:15  and it shall flower as a grape ripe before others. Mine heart was glad therein [or in it], my foot went a right-ful way; from my youth I sought it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:16  I bowed down a little mine ear, and I took it. I found much wisdom in myself,
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:17  and I profited much therein [or much I profited in it]. I shall give glory to him, that giveth wisdom to me.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:18  For why I took counsel to do it; I loved fervently [or greatly](that which is) good, and I shall not be (a)shamed.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:19  My soul wrestled together therein [or in it]; and I was confirmed in doing it. I stretched forth mine hands on high; and my soul shined [or wailed] in the wisdom of him, and he (en)lightened mine uncunnings, (or my unknowings, or my ignorances).
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:20  I (ad)dressed (or directed) my soul to it; and I found it in knowing (or in knowledge).
