I had peaceably from the beginning an heart with those, that is, works, either (en) lightenings of wisdom, [or I welded with them (my) heart from the beginning (or I have joined my heart with it from the beginning)]; for this thing I shall not be forsaken.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:21  My soul was disturbed (or troubled) in seeking it; therefore I shall have peaceably [or shall wield] a good possession.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:22  For why the Lord gave to me a tongue (for) my meed (or my reward); and in (or with) it I shall praise him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:23  Ye untaught men, [cometh] nigh to me; and gather ye you into the house of teaching.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:24  What tarry ye yet? [or What yet ye tarry?] and what say ye in these things? your souls thirst greatly.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:25  I opened my mouth, and I spake, Buy ye wisdom to you (or for your-selves) without silver,
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:26  and make your neck subject to the yoke thereof, and your soul receive teaching, [or and your neck under-layeth to the yoke of it, and your soul undertake discipline]; for why it is in the next to find it.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:27  See ye with your eyes, that I travailed (only) a little, and (then) I found much rest to (or for) me.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:28  Take ye teaching in (or for) much number of silver, and wield ye plenteous gold therein.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:29  Your soul be glad in the mercy of him; and ye shall not be (a)shamed in the praising of him.
ECCLESIASTICUS 51:30  Work ye your work before the time; and he shall give to you your meed (or reward) in his (good) time.
BARUCH 1:1  And these be the words of the book, which Baruch, the son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon;
BARUCH 1:2  in the fifth year, in the seventh day of the month, in the time wherein (the) Chaldeans took Jerusalem, and burnt it with fire.
BARUCH 1:3  And Baruch read the words of this book to the ears of Jeconiah, son of Jehoiakim (or son of Joachim), king of Judah, and to the ears of all the people coming to (hear) the book;
BARUCH 1:4  and to the ears of the mighty [men], (and of the) sons of (the) kings, and to the ears of (the) priests, and to the ears of the people, from the most unto the least of them, of all (those) dwelling in Babylon, and at the flood Sud (or by the Sud River).
BARUCH 1:5  Which heard, and wept, and fasted, and prayed in the sight of the Lord.
BARUCH 1:6  And they gathered money, by [or after] that that each man’s hand might;
BARUCH 1:7  and [they] sent (it) into Jerusalem to Jehoiakim, the (high) priest, the son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the priests, and to all the people that were found with him in Jerusalem;
BARUCH 1:8  when he took (or when he received) the vessels of the temple of the Lord, that were taken away from the temple, to again-call (them) into the land of Judah, in the tenth day of the month Sivan, or May; the silvern [or the silver] vessels, which Zedekiah, the king of Judah, the son of Josiah, (had) made,
BARUCH 1:9  after that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had taken (away) Jeconiah, and (the) princes, and all (the) mighty men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and led them bound into Babylon.
BARUCH 1:10  And they said, Lo! we have sent to you riches [or monies], of (or with) which buy ye burnt sacrifices, and incense, and make ye sacrifice, and offer ye for sin at the altar of your Lord God.
BARUCH 1:11  And pray ye for the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar, his son, that the days of them be on (the) earth as the days of heaven;
BARUCH 1:12  that the Lord give virtue (or strength) to us, and (en)lighten our eyes, that we live under the shadow of Nebuchad-nezzar, king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Belshazzar, his son; and that we serve them by many days, and find grace in the sight of them.
BARUCH 1:13  And pray ye for us to our Lord God, for we have sinned to our Lord God, and his strong vengeance is not turned away from us, till into this day.
BARUCH 1:14  And read ye this book, which we [have] sent to you, to be rehearsed (or to be read aloud) in the temple of the Lord, in a solemn day, and in a covenable day, (or on solemn days, and on other suitable days).
BARUCH 1:15  And ye shall say, Rightfulness [or rightwiseness]is to our Lord God, but shame of our face is to us, as this day (it) is, to all Judah, and to (the) dwellers in Jerusalem,
BARUCH 1:16  to our kings, and to our princes, to our priests, and to our prophets, and to our fathers.
BARUCH 1:17  We sinned before our Lord God,
BARUCH 1:18  and believed not, and trusted not in him. And we were not ready to be subject to him, and we obeyed not to the voice of our Lord God, (so) that we went in his commandments, which he gave to us;
BARUCH 1:19  from the day in which he led our fathers out of the land of Egypt, till into this day, we were unbelieveful to our Lord God; and we were scattered, and went away, (so) that we heard not the voice of him.
BARUCH 1:20  And many evils and cursings, which the Lord ordained to his servant Moses, cleaved to us; which Lord led our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give to us a land flowing (with) milk and honey, as (it is) in this day.
BARUCH 1:21  And we heard not the voice of our Lord God, by [or after] all the words of (the) prophets, which he sent to us, and to our judges;
BARUCH 1:22  and we went away, each man into the wit (or the understanding) of his evil heart, to work to alien gods (or to serve foreign gods), and we did evils before the eyes of our Lord God.
BARUCH 2:1  For which thing our Lord God setted steadfastly his word, which he spake to us, and to our judges, that deemed in Israel, and to our kings, and to our princes, and to all Israel and Judah;
BARUCH 2:2  that the Lord should bring on us great evils, that were not done under heaven, as those be done in Jerusalem; by [or after] those things that be written in the law of Moses,
BARUCH 2:3  that a man should eat the fleshes [or the flesh] of his (own) son, and the fleshes [or the flesh] of his (own) daughter.
BARUCH 2:4  And he gave them into the hand of all (the) kings, that be in our compass, into shame [or reproof], and into desolation in all peoples, among which the Lord scattered us.
BARUCH 2:5  And we be made beneath, and not above; for we sinned to our Lord God, in not obeying to the voice of him.
BARUCH 2:6  Rightfulness [or rightwiseness]is to our Lord God, but shame of face is to us and to our fathers, as this day (it) is.
BARUCH 2:7  For the Lord spake on us all these evils, that came on us.
BARUCH 2:8  And we besought not the face of our Lord God, that we should turn again, each of us from our worst ways.
BARUCH 2:9  And the Lord waked in evils (or watched for evils), and brought those [or them] on us; for the Lord is just [or rightwise] in all his works, which he commanded to us.
BARUCH 2:10  And we heard not the voice of him, that we should go in the commandments of the Lord, which he gave before our face.
BARUCH 2:11  And now, Lord God of Israel, that leddest [or broughtest] thy people out of the land of Egypt in (or with) a strong hand, and in (or with) miracles, and in (or with) great wonders, and in thy great virtue (or with thy great power), and in (or with) an high arm, and madest to thee a name, as this day (it) is;
BARUCH 2:12  we have sinned, we have done unfaithfully, we have done wickedly, our Lord God, in all thy rightfulnesses [or rightwisenesses].
BARUCH 2:13  (Let) Thy wrath be turned away from us; for we be left a few among (the) heathen men, where thou hast scattered us.
BARUCH 2:14  Lord, hear thou our askings, and our prayers, and lead [or bring] us out for thee; and give thou to us to find grace before the face of them, that led us away;
BARUCH 2:15  (so) that all (the) earth know, that thou art our Lord God, and that thy name is called to help on Israel, and on the kin of him (or by his kin).
BARUCH 2:16  Lord, behold thou from thine holy house on us, and bow down thine ear, and hear us.
BARUCH 2:17  Open thine eyes, and see; for not (the) dead men that be in hell (or in the grave), whose spirit is taken from their entrails, shall give honour [or worship] and justifying to the Lord;
BARUCH 2:18  but a soul which is sorry [up] on the greatness [or muchliness] of evil, and goeth bowed, and sick (or feeble), [or meeked], and [the] eyes failing, and an hungry soul [or the soul hunger-ing], giveth glory to thee, and rightful-ness [or rightwiseness] to the Lord.
BARUCH 2:19  For not by [or after] the rightwise-nesses of our fathers we poured out prayers, and asked (for) mercy before thy sight, our Lord God;
BARUCH 2:20  but for thou sentest thy wrath and thy strong vengeance on us, as thou spakest in the hands of thy children (the) prophets (or by thy servants the prophets), and saidest,
BARUCH 2:21  Thus saith the Lord, Bow ye your shoulder[s], and your neck(s), and do ye travail to (or for) the king of Babylon; and ye shall sit in the land, which I gave to your fathers.
BARUCH 2:22  That (or But) if ye do not, neither hear the voice of your Lord God, to work to (or for) the king of Babylon,
BARUCH 2:23  I shall make your failing from the cities of Judah, and from the gates of Jerusalem; and I shall take away from you the voice of gladness [or of mirth], and the voice of joy, and the voice of (the) spouse, and the voice of (the) spousess; and all the land shall be with-out step of them that dwell therein.
BARUCH 2:24  And they heard not thy voice, that they should work to (or for) the king of Babylon; and (so) thou hast set stead-fastly thy words, which thou spakest in the hands of thy children, (the) prophets (or by thy servants the prophets); that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers should be borne over [or translated] from their place.
BARUCH 2:25  And lo! they be cast forth in the heat of the sun, and in the frost of the night; and men[or they] be dead in the worst sorrows, in hunger, and in sword, and in sending out.
BARUCH 2:26  And thou hast set (or brought down low) the temple in which thy name was called to (or for) help, as this day showeth, for the wickedness of the house of Israel, and of the house of Judah.
BARUCH 2:27  And thou, our Lord God, hast done in (or with) us by [or after] all thy goodness, and by all that great merciful doing of thee, [or after all that thy great mercy doing],
BARUCH 2:28  as thou spakest in the hand of thy child Moses (or by thy servant Moses), in the day in which thou command-edest to him to write thy law, before the sons of Israel, and saidest,
BARUCH 2:29  If ye hear not my voice, this great adorning and much [or this great multitude] shall be turned into the least among (the) heathen men, whither I shall scatter them.
BARUCH 2:30  For I knew, that the people shall not hear me, for it is a people of (or with)[an] hard noll. And it (or But they) shall (re)turn to their heart(s) in the land of their captivity;
BARUCH 2:31  and they shall know, that I am the Lord God of them. And I shall give to them an heart, and they shall under-stand, and ears, and they shall hear.
BARUCH 2:32  And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and they shall be mindful of my name.
BARUCH 2:33  [And] They shall turn away them-selves from their hard back, and from their wickednesses; for they shall have mind of [or shall remember] the way of their fathers, that sinned against me.
BARUCH 2:34  And I shall again-call them into the land, which I swore to give to the fathers of them, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and they shall be lords of it. And I shall multiply them, and they [shall] not be made less.
BARUCH 2:35  And I shall ordain to them another testament everlasting, that I be to them into God, and they shall be to me into a people. And I shall no more move my people, the sons of Israel, from the land which I gave to them.
BARUCH 3:1  And now, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in anguishes, and a spirit annoyed (or harmed), crieth to thee.
BARUCH 3:2  Lord, hear thou, and have mercy, for thou art merciful God; and have thou mercy on us, for we have sinned before thee,
BARUCH 3:3  (for) thou sittest without end, and we shall not perish without end.
BARUCH 3:4  Lord God Almighty, God of Israel, hear thou now the prayer of the dead men of Israel, and of the sons of them, that [have] sinned before thee, and heard not the voice of their Lord God, and evils be fastened [or joined] to us.
BARUCH 3:5  Do not thou have mind on (or remember) the wickedness of our fathers, but have thou mind on thine hand, and on thy name, in this time;
BARUCH 3:6  for thou art our Lord God, and, Lord, we shall praise thee.
BARUCH 3:7  For why for this thing thou hast given thy dread in our hearts, (so) that we call (on) thy name to (or for) help, and praise thee in our captivity; for we shall be converted [or turned] from the wickedness of our fathers, that sinned against thee.
BARUCH 3:8  And lo! we be in our captivity today, whither thou scatteredest us, into shame, and into cursing, and into sin, by [or after] all the wickedness of our fathers, that went away from thee, thou our Lord God.
BARUCH 3:9  Israel, hear thou the command-ments of life; perceive thou with ears, (so) that thou know prudence.
BARUCH 3:10  Israel, what (or why) is it, that thou art in the land of (thy) enemies? Thou waxedest (or grewest) eld in an alien land, thou art defouled with dead men,
BARUCH 3:11  (and) thou art areckoned with them, that go down into hell (or the grave)?
BARUCH 3:12  Thou hast forsaken the well of wisdom;
BARUCH 3:13  for why if thou haddest gone in the ways of God, soothly thou haddest dwelled in peace on (the) earth.
BARUCH 3:14  Learn thou, where is wisdom, where is prudence, where is virtue, where is understanding, (so) that thou know (al)together, where is long enduring of life, and lifelode, (or livelihood), (and) where is (the) light of (the) eyes, and peace.
BARUCH 3:15  Who found the place thereof, and who entered into the treasures thereof?
BARUCH 3:16  Where be the princes of (the) heathen men, and that be lords over the beasts, that be on (the) earth?
BARUCH 3:17  Which played with the birds of heaven; which treasure silver and gold, in which men trust, and none end [there] is of the purchasing of them?
BARUCH 3:18  Which make silver, and be busy, and no finding is of their works?
BARUCH 3:19  They be destroyed, and went down to hells, [or to hell], (or to the grave); and other men rose (up) in the place of them.
BARUCH 3:20  The young men of them saw light, and dwelled on (the) earth. But they knew not the way of wisdom,
BARUCH 3:21  neither understood the paths thereof; neither the sons of them received it. It was made far from the face of them;
BARUCH 3:22  it is not heard (of) in the land of Canaan, neither [it] is seen in Teman.
BARUCH 3:23  Also the sons of Hagar, that sought out prudence which is of (or on the) earth, the merchants of (the) earth, and of Teman, and the tale tellers [or the fablers, or janglers], and seekers out of prudence, and of understand-ing. But they knew not the way of wisdom, neither had mind on the paths thereof.
BARUCH 3:24  O! Israel, the house of God is full great, and the place of his possession is great;
BARUCH 3:25  it is great and hath none end, high and great without measure.
BARUCH 3:26  (The) Named giants were there; they that were of great stature at the beginning, and knew (or knowing in) battle.
BARUCH 3:27  The Lord chose not these, neither they found the way of wisdom [or of discipline]; therefore they perished.
BARUCH 3:28  And for they had not wisdom, they perished for their unwisdom.
BARUCH 3:29  Who ascended, or went up, into heaven, and took that wisdom, and brought it down from the clouds?
BARUCH 3:30  Who (hath) passed over the sea, and found it, and brought it more than chosen gold?
BARUCH 3:31  None is [or There is not], that may know the way thereof, neither that seeketh [out] the paths thereof;
BARUCH 3:32  but he that have all things [or that knoweth all things], knew it, and found it by his prudence. Which made ready the earth in everlasting time, and filled it with two-footed beasts, and (with) four-footed beasts.
BARUCH 3:33  Which sendeth out (the) light, and it goeth, and called it (again); and it obeyeth to him in trembling.
BARUCH 3:34  Forsooth (the) stars gave light in their keepings, and were glad; those [or they] were called, and those said, We be present [or they said, We come to (thee)]; and those (or they) shined to him with mirth, that made those [or them].
BARUCH 3:35  This is our God, and none other shall be guessed against him.
BARUCH 3:36  This [or He] found each way of wisdom, and gave it to Jacob, his child (or his servant), and to Israel, his darling [or his dearworth(y)].
BARUCH 3:37  After these things he was seen in (many) lands, and lived with men.
BARUCH 4:1  This (is the) book of God’s behests [or commandments], and the law which is without end. All that hold it, shall come to life. But they that have forsaken it, shall come into death.
BARUCH 4:2  Jacob, be thou converted, and take thou (hold of)[or catch] it; go thou [or walk] by the way at the brightness thereof, against the light thereof.
BARUCH 4:3  Give thou not thy glory to another, and thy dignity to an alien, (or to a strange, or foreign) folk.
BARUCH 4:4  Israel, we be blessed; for those things that please God, be open to us [or be known to us].
BARUCH 4:5  The people of God, Israel worthy to be had in mind (or remembered), be thou patienter, either of better comfort.
BARUCH 4:6  Ye be sold to (the) heathen men, not into perdition; but for that that ye in ire [or wrath] stirred God to wrath-fulness, ye be betaken to adversaries.
BARUCH 4:7  For ye wrathed that God ever-lasting, that made you; and ye offered to fiends, and not to God. [Forsooth ye stirred to bitterness the everlasting God, that made you; offering to devils, and not to God.]
BARUCH 4:8  For ye forgot him that nourished or nursed you, and ye made sorry [or sorrowful] your nurse, Jerusalem.
BARUCH 4:9  For it saw (the) wrathfulness of God coming to you, and it said, Ye nigh coasts of Zion, hear; forsooth God hath brought great mourning to me.
BARUCH 4:10  For I saw the captivity of my people, of my sons and daughters, which he that is without beginning and end [or the Everlasting] brought on them.
BARUCH 4:11  For I nourished them with mirth; but I left them (or I let them go) with weeping and mourning.
BARUCH 4:12  No man have joy on (or over) me, a widow and desolate. I am forsaken [or left] of (or by) many, for the sins of my sons; for they bowed away from the law of God.
BARUCH 4:13  Forsooth they knew not (the) right-fulnesses of him; neither they went [or walked] by the ways of God’s behests (or commandments), neither by the paths of his truth they entered with rightfulness [or rightwiseness].
BARUCH 4:14  The nigh coasts of Zion come, and have they mind on, [or bethink they (of)], (or remember) the captivity of my sons and daughters, which he that is without beginning and end [or the Everlasting] brought on them.
BARUCH 4:15  For he brought on them a folk from (a)far, an evil folk, and of another lan-guage; that reverenced not an eld [or an old] man, neither had mercy on children;
BARUCH 4:16  and they led away the dear-worthy sons of a widow, and made a woman alone desolate of sons.
BARUCH 4:17  But what may I help you? (or How can I help you?)
BARUCH 4:18  For he that brought on you evils, shall deliver you from the hands of your enemies.
BARUCH 4:19  Go ye, sons, go ye; for I am forsaken, or I am left alone.
BARUCH 4:20  I have unclothed me of the stole, either long robe, of peace; but I have clothed me with a sackcloth of beseeching, and I shall cry to the Highest in my days.
BARUCH 4:21  Sons, be ye of better comfort [or be of better heart, or stabler]; cry ye to the Lord, and he shall deliver you from the hand of princes, that be your enemies.
BARUCH 4:22  For I hoped (for) your health without end, and joy came to me from the Holy (One) on (or for the) mercy, that shall come to you from your Saviour without beginning and end [or your Saviour Everlasting].
BARUCH 4:23  For I sent you out with mourning and weeping; but God shall bring [or shall lead] you again to me, with joy and mirth without end.
BARUCH 4:24  For as the neighbouresses [or the neighbours] of Zion saw your captivity made of (or by) God, so they shall see and in swiftness [or in haste] your health of (or your deliverance from our) God, which health (or deliverance) shall come to you from above, with great honour and everlasting shining.
BARUCH 4:25  Sons, suffer ye patiently (the) ire [or the wrath] that came on you; for thine enemy pursued thee, but thou shalt see soon the perdition of him [or soon thou shalt see the perdition of him], and thou shalt ascend (or go) upon the necks of him.
BARUCH 4:26  My delicate men went (in) sharp ways; for they as a flock that is ravished were led (away) of (or by the) enemies. [My delicates, or nourished in delights, walked sharp ways; soothly they were led as a flock ravished with enemies.]
BARUCH 4:27  Sons, be ye patienter [or of evener heart, or stabler], and cry ye [a] far to the Lord; for why your mind shall be of (or on) him that leadeth you.
BARUCH 4:28  For as your wit was, that ye erred from God, ye shall convert again, and shall seek him ten times so much (the more).
BARUCH 4:29  For he that brought in evils to you, shall bring again everlasting mirth to you with your health (or your deliverance).
BARUCH 4:30  Jerusalem, be thou of better com-fort; for he that named thee, exciteth thee. [Jerusalem, be thou more stable, or of better heart; soothly he that named thee, admonisheth thee.]
BARUCH 4:31  They that travailed thee, shall perish guilty; and they that thanked, [or joyed], in (or at) thy falling, shall be punished.
BARUCH 4:32  [The] Cities to which thy sons served, shall be punished, and that city that took thy sons, shall be punished.
BARUCH 4:33  For as Babylon made joy in thy hurling down [or in thy falling], and was glad in thy fall, so it shall be made sorry [or it shall be sorrowful] in his (or its own) desolation.
BARUCH 4:34  And the full out joy of the multitude thereof shall be cut away, and the joy thereof shall be into mourning.
BARUCH 4:35  For why fire shall come on it from him that is without beginning and end [or (from) the Everlasting], in full long days; and it shall be inhabited of (or by) fiends [or devils], into the multitude [or (the) muchliness] of time.
BARUCH 4:36  Jerusalem, behold about to the east, and see thou (the) mirth coming of (or from) God to thee.
BARUCH 4:37  For lo! thy sons come, which [or whom] thou leftest (or thou lettest go) scattered; they come gathered from the east unto the west, in (or by) the word of the Holy (One), and make joy [or joying] to the honour of God.
BARUCH 5:1  Jerusalem, unclothe thee of the stole of thy mourning, and travailing [or of thy travail]; and clothe thou thee in [or with] the fairness, and (the) honour of it, which is of (or from) God to thee in everlasting glory [or that is to thee of (or from) God in everlasting glory].
BARUCH 5:2  God of rightfulness [or rightwise-ness] shall (en)compass thee with a double cloth (or a double cloak), and shall set [or put] on thine head a mitre of everlasting honour.
BARUCH 5:3  For God shall show his brightness in (or to) thee, which is under heaven.
BARUCH 5:4  For thy name shall be named of (or by) God to thee without end, The peace of rightfulness [or rightwise-ness], and The honour of piety.
BARUCH 5:5  Jerusalem, rise up, and stand in an high place [or stand in (or on) high], and behold about to the east; and see thy sons gathered together from the sun rising till to the west, in (or by) the word of the Holy (One), that make joy in the mind of God.
BARUCH 5:6  For they went out from thee, and were led (away) of enemies on feet (or were led away on foot by their enemies); but the Lord shall bring to thee them borne into honour, as the sons of (the) realm [or the sons of (the) kingdom].
BARUCH 5:7  For God hath ordained to make low each high hill, and (the) ever-lasting rocks of stones, and great valleys, to fill the unevenness of (the) earth; (so) that Israel (may) go diligently into the honour of God.
BARUCH 5:8  Forsooth the woods, and each tree of sweetness, (over)shadowed Israel, by the commandment of God.
BARUCH 5:9  For God shall bring Israel with mirth, into [or in] the light of his majesty, with mercy and rightfulness [or right-wiseness], which is of (or from) him.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:1  Here beginneth a sample of the epistle of the same Baruch, which epistle Jeremy (or Jeremiah) sent to the Jews, that were led away (as) prisoners into Babylon, of (or by) the king of (the) Babylonians, that he should tell to them, by that that was commanded of (or by) God to him[or after that it is commanded to him of (or by) God].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:2  For the sins which ye sinned before God, ye shall be led (away as) prisoners [or (as) captives] into Babylon, of (or by) Nebuchadnezzar, king of (the) Babylonians.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:3  Therefore ye shall enter into Babylon [or And so ye go into Babylon], and ye shall be there full many years, and into (a) long time, till to seven generations; forsooth after this I shall lead out you from thence with peace.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:4  But now ye shall see in Babylon gods of gold, and of silver, and of stone, and of tree (or of wood), to be borne on shoulders, showing dread to (the) heathen men [or to (the) folks].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:5  Therefore see ye, lest also ye be made like [to] alien deeds, and lest ye dread, and [that] dread take you in them. Therefore when ye see a company behind and before (them), worship ye God, [or And so the company of people seen from behind (them) and from before worshipping (them)],
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:6  (then) say in your hearts, Lord God, it behooveth that thou be worshipped [or it behooveth thee for to be worshipped].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:7  Forsooth mine angel is with you, but (or and) I shall seek your souls [or (and) I myself shall seek out your souls].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:8  For why the trees (or the wood) of them be polished of (or by) a carpenter; also they be arrayed with gold, and arrayed with silver, and be false [or they also engolded and ensilvered be false], and may not (or be not able to) speak.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:9  And as to a virgin [or to a maiden] loving ornaments, so, when gold is taken, ornaments be made to (or for the) idols. Certainly the gods of them have golden crowns on their heads;
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:10  wherefore priests withdraw from those gods gold and silver, and spend it in (or on) themselves.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:11  Soothly they give also of that to whores, and array [or adorn] whores; and again when they receive that of (or from) whores, they array [or they adorn] their gods.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:12  But those [or these]gods be not delivered from rust and moths. For-sooth when they be covered with a cloth (or a cloak) of purple,
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:13  priests shall wipe the face(s) of them, for (the) dust of the house (or because of the dust of the temple), which is full much among those gods[or that is full much among them].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:14  Forsooth (these)idols have a sceptre, [or (a) king’s rod], as a man hath; (yea), as the judge of a country, (but) that slayeth not a man sinning against himself.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:15  Also they have in the hand a sword, and an ax; but they deliver not themselves from battle and from thieves.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:16  Wherefore be it known to you, that they be not gods; therefore worship (or dread) ye not them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:17  For as a broken vessel of a man is made unprofitable, such also be the gods of them. When they be set (up) in the house (or in the temple), the eyes of them be full of dust, of (or from) the feet of men entering [in].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:18  And as [the] gates be set about a man, that offended the king, either as when a dead man is brought to the sepulchre, so priests keep securely the doors with closings, and locks, lest they be robbed of (or by) thieves.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:19  They tend lanterns to (or for) them, and soothly many lanterns, of which they may or be able to see none;
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:20  forsooth they be as (the) beams in an house (or in the temple). Soothly men say that (the) serpents, that be of (the) earth, lick out the hearts of them; (yet) while the serpents eat them, and their cloth(es)[or (the) clothing of them], and they feel it not.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:21  The faces of them be black of (or from) the smoke, which is made in the house (or in the temple).
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:22  Night crows (or bats) and swallows fly above the body (or the bodies) of them, and above the head(s) of them, and birds also, and cats (sit upon them) in like manner.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:23  Wherefore know ye, that they be not gods; therefore dread ye not them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:24  Also the gold which they have, is to (or for their) fairness; no but some man wipe away the rust, they shall not shine. For they (even) feeled (it) not, the while those were welled together [or Forsooth neither (even) the while they were molten together, they feeled (it)].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:25  They be bought of all price (or for a very high price), in which no spirit (or breath) is in them. [They be bought of all price, in which things spirit is not in them.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:26  They without feet be borne on (the) shoulders of men, and show openly their unnobility to men;
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:27  be they shamed also that worship them. Therefore if they fall down to (the) earth, they shall not rise (up) of (or by) themselves; and if any man setteth that idol upright, it shall not stand by itself, but as to (or for) dead things [or as to (or for) dead men] shoulders shall (or must) be put to them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:28  The priests of them sell the sacrifices of them, and mis-use; in like manner and the women of them ravish [or taking] away, neither to a sick man, neither to a beggar, they give anything.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:29  Of their sacrifices foul women, and in unclean blood, touch. There-fore know ye by these things, that they be not gods, and dread ye not them. [Of the sacrifices of them women with child, and menstruate, or in unclean blood, touch (al)together. And so witting of these things, for they be not gods, dread ye them not.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:30  For whereof be they called gods? For women set sacrifices to gods of silver, and of gold, and of tree (or of wood);
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:31  and (the) priests that have coats rent, and (their) heads and beard(s) shaven, whose heads be naked, sit in the houses of them (or in their temples). [and in the houses of them sit (the) priests having torn, or cut, coats, and heads and beard(s) shaven, whose heads be naked.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:32  Soothly they roar and cry against (or before) their gods, as in (or at) the supper of a dead man.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:33  (And the) Priests take away the clothes of them, and clothe their wives, and their children.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:34  And if they suffer anything of evil of (or from) any man, or if they suffer anything of good, they may not (or be not able to) yield back (or to repay it). Neither they may or be able to ordain [or (to) make] a king, neither do (him) away.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:35  In like manner they may neither give riches, neither yield evil [thing]. If any man maketh a vow to them, and yieldeth not, they ask not (for) this [or If any man shall avow to them, and shall not yield, neither they require, or ask, (for) this thing].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:36  They deliver not a man from death, neither ravish a sick (or a weak) man from a mightier [or neither deliver a sick man from a more mighty].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:37  They restore not a blind man to sight; they shall not deliver a man from need.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:38  They shall not have mercy on a widow, neither they shall do good to fatherless children.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:39  Their gods of tree (or of wood), and of stone, and of gold, and of silver, be like (the) stones of the mountain; forsooth they that worship them, shall be shamed [or shall be confounded].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:40  How therefore is it to guess, either to say [or to be said], that they be gods? for why yet when (even the) Chaldeans honour not them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:41  Which when they hear that a dumb man may not speak, offer him to Bel, and ask of him to (be able to) speak; as if they that have no stirring, may or be able to feel.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:42  And they, when they shall under-stand, shall forsake those idols; for those gods of them have no wit.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:43  Forsooth women gird (about) with ropes [or cords] sit in ways, and kindled (or burned) bones of olives. Soothly when any of these women is drawn away of (or by) any man passing, and sleepeth with him, she despiseth her neighbouress, that she is not had worthy as herself, neither her rope [or her cord] is broken.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:44  Forsooth all things that be done to them, be false. How therefore is it to guess, either to say, that those (or that they) be gods? [or How is it to be guessed, or to be said, them to be gods?]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:45  Forsooth those idols be made of (or by) smiths [or carpenters], and of (or by) goldsmiths. They shall be none other thing, no but that that (the) priests will (or desire) that they be [or that (the) priests will for to be].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:46  Also those goldsmiths that make them, be not of much time; therefore whether those things [or the things] that be made of (or by) them, may be or be able to be gods?
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:47  Soothly they left false things, and shame (or reproof) to men to coming afterward [or coming after].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:48  For why when battles and evils come on them, priests think, where they shall hide themselves with those [or with them].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:49  How therefore owe (or ought) those [or they] to be deemed, that they be gods, which neither deliver them-selves from battle, neither deliver themselves from evils?
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:50  For why when those [or they] be of tree (or of wood), and of stone, and of gold, and of silver, it shall be known afterward,
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:51  of (or by) all folks, and kings, that those things be false, that be made open; for those be not gods, but the works of (the) hands of men, and no work of God is with (or is in) them. [to all folks and kings; which be open, or known, for they be not gods, but (the) works of men’s hands, and no work of God (is) with (or is in) them.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:52  Whereof therefore it is known, that they be not gods, but the works of (the) hands of men [or but (the) works of men’s hands], and no work of God is in them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:53  They raise not a king to a country, neither shall give rain to men.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:54  Also they shall not deem [or judge](a) doom, neither they shall deliver the country from wrong. For those be able to (do) nothing [or For they may (do) nothing], as little crows betwixt the midst of heaven and of (the) earth.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:55  For when fire falleth into the house of gods of tree (or of wood), and of gold, and of silver, soothly the priests of those [or the priests of them] shall flee, and shall be delivered; but they shall be burnt as (the) beams in the midst.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:56  Forsooth they shall not against-stand a king and battle. How there-fore is it to guess, or to receive, that they be gods? [or How therefore is it to be guessed, or to be received, for they be gods?]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:57  Gods of tree (or of wood), and of stone, and of gold, and of silver, shall not deliver themselves from night thieves, neither from day thieves, and wicked men be stronger than those gods.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:58  They shall take away gold, and silver, and cloth(es), by which those [or they] be covered, and (then) they shall go away; neither they (be able to) help themselves.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:59  Therefore it is better to be a king showing his virtue (or his power), either [or (else)] a profitable vessel in the house, in which he shall have glory that wieldeth it, than false gods; either [or (else)] a door in the house, that keepeth those things that be in it, is better than false gods.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:60  Forsooth the sun, and moon, and stars, when they be bright [or when they be shining], and sent out to profits, obey.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:61  In like manner and [the] light-ning, when it appeareth, is clear. Soothly the same thing and (the) wind breatheth in each country.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:62  And (the) clouds, to which, when it is commanded of (or by) God to go through all the world, perform that, that is commanded to those [or do what thing is commanded to them].
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:63  Also (the) fire sent from above, to waste mountains and woods, doeth that, that is commanded to it [or doeth what thing is commanded to it]; but these idols be not like to one of those things, neither by forms, neither by virtues (or in power).
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:64  Wherefore it is neither to guess, neither to say, that they be gods, when they may not (or be not able to) neither deem doom, neither do (good) to men. [Whereof neither it is to be guessed, neither to be said, them for to be gods, when they may neither deem doom, neither do to men.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:65  Therefore know ye that those be not gods, and dread ye not them. [And so witting for they be not gods, therefore ye shall not dread them.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:66  For they shall neither curse, neither bless kings.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:67  Also they show not to (the) heathen men signs in (the) heaven(s), neither those [or they] shall shine as the sun, neither they shall give light as the moon.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:68  Beasts that may or be able to flee under a roof, and do profit to them-selves, be better than they. [Beasts be better than they, which may flee under a roof, and profit to themselves.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:69  Therefore by no manner it is open to you, that they be gods. For which thing, dread ye not them.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:70  For why as a man of rags, or shoeless, in a place where gourds [or cucumbers, that be bitter herbs], waxed, keepeth nothing, so be their gods of tree (or of wood), and of silver, and of gold.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:71  In the same manner and a white-thorn (bush) in a garden [or in a yard]keepeth nothing, on which thorn each bird sitteth, (and) in like manner and their gods of tree (or of wood), and of gold, and of silver, be like [to] a dead man cast forth in(to)(the) darknesses.
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:72  Also of purple and of marble, which they hold above it; therefore ye shall know, that they be not gods. Also those be eaten at the last, and it shall be into shame in the country. [And of the purple and marble, that they hold above them(selves), ye shall know also, for they be no gods. Also at the last they themselves be eaten, and it shall be into reproof in the country.]
EPISTLE OF JEREMIAH 1:73  Better is a just man, that hath no simulacra, for why he shall be far from shames (or reproofs).
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:1  And they walked in the midst of the flame, and praised God, and blessed the Lord. [And they walked in the middle of the flame, praising God, and blessing the Lord.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:2  Forsooth Azariah stood, and prayed thus; and he opened his mouth in the midst of the fire, and said,
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:3  Lord, God of our fathers, thou art blessed, and worthy to be praised, and thy name is glorious into worlds; [Blessed art thou, Lord God of our Fathers, and praiseful, or worthy to be praised, and thy name glorious into worlds;]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:4  for thou art rightful in all (the) things which thou didest to us, and all thy works be true; and thy ways be rightful [or right], and thy dooms (or thy judgements)be true.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:5  For thou hast done true dooms, by [or after] all (the) things which thou broughtest in on us, and on Jeru-salem, the holy city of our fathers; for in truth and in doom, thou broughtest in all these things for our sins.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:6  For we sinned, and did wickedly, going away from thee,
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:7  and we trespassed in all things, and we heard not, neither kept thy commandments, neither we did as thou commandedest to us, (so) that it should be well to (or with) us. [and trespassed in all things, and heard not thine behests, neither kept (them), neither did as thou commandedest to us, that it were well to us.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:8  Therefore thou didest by thy very doom (or in thy true judgement) all (the) things which thou broughtest in on us, and all (the) things which thou didest to us; [Therefore all (the) things that thou leddest in upon us, and all (the) things that thou didest to us, in very doom thou hast done;]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:9  and thou hast betaken us in(to) the hands of (our) enemies, wicked men, and worst trespassers, and to the unjust king, and worst over all (the) earth.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:10  And now we may not (or we be not able to) open the mouth; we be made (a) shame and (a) reproof to thy servants, and to them that worship thee.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:11  We beseech (thee), give thou not us to (our) enemies without end, for thy name, and destroy thou not thy testament (or thy covenant), [We pray, betake not us into without end, for thy name, and destroy not thy testament,]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:12  and take thou not away thy mercy from us, for Abraham, thy darling [or thy dearworthy], and Isaac, thy servant, and Israel, [or Jacob], thine holy (one);
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:13  to which thou spakest, promising that thou shouldest multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and as (the) gravel which is in (or on) the brink of the sea.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:14  For why, Lord, we be made little, more than all folks, and we be low in all (the) earth today, for our sins. [For, Lord, we be made little, more than all heathen men, and we be meek, or low, in each land this day, for our sins.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:15  And in this time is no prince [or And there is not in this time prince], and (or) duke, and (or) prophet, neither burnt sacrifice, neither sacrifice, neither offering, neither incense, neither place of first fruits before thee, (so) that we may or we be able to find thy mercy;
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:16  but be we received in (or with a) contrite soul, and in (or with a) spirit of meekness.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:17  As in (the) burnt sacrifice of rams, and of bulls, and as in thousands of fat lambs, so our sacrifice be made today in thy sight, that it please thee; for no shame [or confusion] is to them that trust in thee.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:18  And now we pursue (or follow) thee in (or with) all the heart, and we dread thee, and we seek thy face.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:19  Shame thou not us, but do with us by [or after] thy mildness, and by [or after] the multitude of thy mercy.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:20  And deliver thou us in thy marvels, and give thou glory to thy name, Lord; and all men be (a)shamed, that show evils to thy servants;
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:21  be they shamed in all thy might (or in all their might), and the strength of them be all-broken; [be they confounded in all thy power (or in all their power), and the strength of them be broken (al)together;]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:22  and they shall know, that thou art the Lord God alone, and glorious on (or over) the roundness of (the) lands [or the roundness of (the) earth’s]. (Amen).
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:23  And the ministers (or the servants) of the king, that had sent them (in), ceased not to make hot the furnace with cement [or naphtha], and hards of flax [or of hemp], and pitch, and scions [or cuttings] of vines.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:24  And the flame was shed [or poured] out over the furnace by nine and forty cubits,
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:25  and brake out, and burnt them that it found of (the) Chaldeans beside the furnace. [and brake out, and burnt whom of (the) Chaldeans it found beside the furnace.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:26  Forsooth the angel of the Lord came down with Azariah and his fellows, into the furnace, and smote out the flame of the fire from the furnace;
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:27  and made the midst of the furnace as the wind of dew blowing; and utterly the fire touched not them, neither made sorry, neither did anything of dis-ease [or neither made sorrowful, neither brought in anything of heaviness].
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:28  Then these three as of one mouth praised and glorified God, and blessed God in the furnace, and said,
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:29  Lord God of our fathers, thou art blessed, and worthy to be praised, and glorious, and above enhanced into worlds (or for evermore); [Blessed art thou, Lord God of our fathers, and worthy to be praised, and glorious, and above enhanced into worlds;]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:30  and blessed is the name of thy glory, which name is holy, and worthy to be praised, and above enhanced in(to) all worlds. [and blessed (is) the name of thy glory, the which is holy, and worthy to be praised, and above raised in(to) all worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:31  Thou art blessed in the holy temple of thy glory, and above praiseable, and glorious into worlds. [Blessed art thou in the holy temple of thy glory, and thou above praiseful, and glorious into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:32  Thou art blessed in (or on) the throne of thy realm, and above praiseable, and above enhanced into worlds. [Blessed art thou in the throne of thy realm, and above praiseful, and above raised into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:33  Thou art blessed, that beholdest (the) depths of (the) waters, and sittest on cherubim, and praiseable, and above enhanced into worlds. [Blessed art thou, that beholdest (the) deepness-es, and sittest upon cherubim, and praiseful, and above raised into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:34  Thou art blessed in the firmament of heaven, and praiseable, and glorious into worlds. [Blessed art thou in the firmament of heaven, and praiseful, and glorious into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:35  All (the) works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance (or raise) ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:36  Angels of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:37  Heavens, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:38  All (the) waters that be above (the) heavens, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:39  All the virtues of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds. (All the hosts or the powers of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and exalt him above all for evermore.)
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:40  Sun and moon, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:41  Stars of heaven, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:42  Rain and dew, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:43  Each spirit of God, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:44  Fire and heat, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:45  Cold and summer, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:46  Dews and white frost, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:47  Black frost and cold, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance ye him into worlds. [Binding frost and cold, bless ye to the Lord; praise ye, and above raise ye him into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:48  Ices and snows, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:49  Nights and days, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:50  Light and darkness, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:51  Lightnings and clouds, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:52  The earth bless the Lord; praise it, and above enhance it him [or above raise (ye) him] into worlds. (The earth, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and exalt ye him above all for evermore.)
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:53  Mountains and little hills, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:54  All burgeoning things in (the) earth, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:55  Wells, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:56  Seas and floods (or Seas and rivers), bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:57  Whales, and all things that be moved in (the) waters (or Whales, and all things that move in the waters), bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:58  All birds of the air, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance ye him into worlds. [All fowls of heaven, bless ye to the Lord; praise ye, and above raise ye him into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:59  All wild beasts and tame beasts, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance ye him into worlds. [All beasts and eatable (or edible), or little, beasts, bless ye to the Lord; praise ye, and above raise ye him into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:60  Sons of men, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:61  Israel bless the Lord; praise it, and above enhance it him [or above raise (ye) him] into worlds. (Israel, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and exalt ye him above all for evermore.)
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:62  Priests of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:63  Servants of the Lord, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:64  Spirits and souls of just men, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance [or raise] ye him into worlds.
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:65  Holy men and meek of heart, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance ye him into worlds. [Holy and meek in heart, bless ye to the Lord; praise ye, and above raise ye him into worlds.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:66  Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless ye the Lord; praise ye, and above enhance ye him into worlds. The which Lord ravished us from hell, and saved (us) from the hand of death, and delivered us from the midst of flame burning, and ravished us from the midst of (the) fire, (or The which Lord delivered us from the grave, and saved us from the hand of death, and delivered us from the midst of the burning flame, yea, delivered us from the midst of the fire). [Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless ye to the Lord; praise ye, and above raise ye him into worlds. Which delivered us from hell, and made safe from the hand of death, and delivered from the middle of the burning flame, and ravished us out of the middle of the fire.]
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:67  Acknowledge ye to the Lord, for he is good; for his mercy is into the worlds (or for evermore).
PRAYER OF AZARIAH & SONG OF THE THREE 1:68  All religious men [or All (the) religious], bless ye the Lord, God of gods; praise ye, and acknowledge to him, for his mercy is into all worlds (or for evermore).
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:1  Here beginneth an epistle of (or about) holy Susanna. In those days a man was in Babylon, and his name was Joakim./A man was in Babylon, and his name was Joakim.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:2  And he took a wife, Susanna by name, the daughter of Hilkiah, a woman full fair, and dreading the Lord.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:3  Forsooth her father and mother, when they were rightful [or just], taught their daughter by [or after] the law of Moses.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:4  Soothly Joakim was full rich, and had a garden nigh his house; and the Jews came to him, for he was the most worshipful [or more honourable] of (or than) all (the others).
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:5  And twain eld men [or two old men] were ordained to be judges in that year, of which the Lord spake, that wickedness went out of Babylon, of (or from) the elder judges, that seemed to govern the people.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:6  These judges used often the house of Joakim; and all men that had dooms came to them. [These often haunted the house of Joakim; and all that had dooms came to them.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:7  Forsooth when the people had (re)turned again (home) after midday, Susanna entered, and walked in the garden of her husband.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:8  And the (two) elder men saw her entering each day, and walking; and they burnt out into the covetousness or concupiscence of (or for) her. [And the (two) elder men saw her each day entering, and walking; and they burned in the covetousness of her.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:9  And they turned away their wit, and bowed down [or bowed away] their eyes, (so) that they saw not heaven, neither bethought on just dooms.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:10  Soothly both were wounded by the love of (or for) her, and they showed not their sorrow to them-selves together (or to each other);
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:11  for they were ashamed to show to themselves (or to each other) their covetousness or concupiscence, will-ing (or desiring) to lie fleshly by [or with] her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:12  And they espied each day more busily to see her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:13  And the one said to the tother, Go we home, for the hour of meat is.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:14  And they went out, and parted from themselves. And when they had (re)turned again, they came into one place (or But then they returned again, and they came to the same place); and they asked each of (the) other (or each other) the cause, and they acknowledged their covetousness. And then in common they ordained a time, when they might find her alone.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:15  Forsooth it was done, when they espied a covenable (or an opportune) day, she entered sometime, as yester-day and the third day ago, with two damsels alone, and would be washed in the garden; for why heat was (or it was hot).
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:16  And there was not any man (there), or And no man was there, except the two eld men [or (the) two old men] hid (there), beholding her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:17  Therefore she said to the damsels, Bring ye to me oil, and ointments; and close the doors of the garden, (so) that I (can) be washed. [And she said to the maidens, Bring ye to me oil, and soap, or ointment; and shut ye the doors of the garden, that I be washed.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:18  And they did as she commanded; and they closed the doors of the garden, and went out by a postern (or by a back door), to bring those things that she had commanded. And they knew not, that the (two) eld men were hid within.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:19  Soothly when the damsels were gone out, (the) twain eld men rised (up)[or the two old men rose (up)], and ran to her, and said,
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:20  Lo! the doors of the garden be closed, and no man seeth us, and we be in the covetousness or concupis-cence of (or for) thee. Wherefore assent thou to us, and be thou meddled (or mingled) with us, [or Wherefore accord to us, and be joined with us].
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:21  And if thou wilt not, we shall say witnessing against thee, that a young man was with thee, and for this cause thou sentest out the damsels from thee.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:22  And Susanna inwardly sorrowed, and said, Anguishes be to me on each side; for if I do this [thing], death is to me; forsooth if I do (it) not, I shall not escape your hands.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:23  But it is better for me to fall into your hands, without work, than to do sin [or to sin] in the sight of the Lord.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:24  And (then) Susanna cried with (a) great (or with a loud) voice, but also the eld men [or the old men] cried (out) against her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:25  Forsooth one ran [or Soothly the one ran], and opened the door of (or to) the garden.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:26  Soothly when the servants of the house had heard the cry in the garden, they fell in by the postern (or by the back door), to see what it was.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:27  But after that the eld men [or the old men] spake, the servants were ashamed greatly, for never was such a word said of (or about) Susanna.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:28  And the morrow day was made. And when the people was come to Joakim, her husband, also the two priests (or the two eld men) full of wicked thoughts came against Susanna, for to slay her. [And the morrow day is made. And when the people came to her husband Joakim, and the two priests (or the two old men) came full of evil thought against Susanna, for to slay her.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:29  And they said before all the people, Send ye to Susanna (or Send for Susanna), the daughter of Hilkiah, the wife of Joakim. And anon (or at once) they sent (for her).
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:30  And she came with her father, and mother, and children, and all [her] kinsmen.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:31  And certainly Susanna was full delicate, either tender, and fair of shape [or form].
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:32  And those wicked men command-ed, that she should be uncovered, for she was covered; that namely so (or so that namely) they should be filled of [or with] her fairness.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:33  Therefore her kinsmen[or her nigh friends] wept, and all that knew her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:34  Forsooth the two priests (or the two old men) rised together in the midst of the people, and set [or putted] their hands on the head of her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:35  And she wept, and beheld to heaven, for her heart had trust in the Lord. [Which weeping beheld to heaven, forsooth the heart of her was having trust in the Lord.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:36  And the priests (or the two old men) said, When we walked alone in the garden, this Susanna entered with two damsels [or with two maidens]; and she closed the door of the garden, and let go the damsels.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:37  And a young man, that was hid, came to her, and lay by her [or did lechery with her].
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:38  Certainly when we were in a corner of the garden, we saw the wickedness, and ran to them, [For-sooth we, when we were in a corner of the garden, seeing the wickedness, ran to them,]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:39  and we saw them meddled together. And soothly we might not take (hold of)[or catch] him, for he was stronger than we; and when he had opened the doors, he skipped out [or he leapt out].
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:40  But when we had taken (hold of) this woman, we asked, who was the young man; and she would not show to us. Of this thing we be witnesses.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:41  The multitude believed to them, as to (or because they were) the elder men and judges of the people, and condemned her to death.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:42  Forsooth Susanna cried loud with (a) great voice, and said, Lord God, without beginning and end [or Lord God everlasting], thou art or that art (the) knower of hid things, that know-est all things before that they be done [or be made];
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:43  thou knowest, that they have borne false witnessing against me. And lo! I die, when I have not done any of these things, which these men have made (out) maliciously against me.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:44  Forsooth the Lord heard the voice of her.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:45  And when she was led to the death, the Lord raised (up) the holy spirit of a young child (or of a young man), whose name was Daniel.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:46  And he cried (out) loud with a great voice, I am clean of (or I am clear from) the blood of this woman.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:47  And all the people turned again to(wards) him [or And all the people together turned to him], and said, What is this word, which thou hast spoken?
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:48  And when he stood in the midst of them, he said, So ye, fond children of Israel, [or So ye, fools, sons of Israel], not deeming neither knowing that that is true, (have) condemned the daughter of Israel.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:49  Turn ye again to the doom (or Return to the judgement seat), for they spake false witnessing against her. [Turn ye again to doom, for they have spoken false witnessing against her.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:50  Therefore the people (re)turned again with haste. And the (other) eld [or old] men of the people, not those two priests(or not those two old men), said to him, Come thou, and sit in the midst of us, and show (it) to us; for God hath given to thee the honour of (an) elder.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:51  And Daniel said to them, Part ye (or Separate) them atwain afar, [or each from (the) other], and I shall deem them.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:52  Therefore, when they were parted one from the other, he called one of them, and said to him, Thou eld man of evil days, now thy sins be come, which thou wroughtest before [or Thou old (man) of evil days, now thy sins come on thee, which thou wroughtest before],
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:53  deeming unjust dooms, oppress-ing innocents, and delivering (or free-ing) guilty men, when the Lord saith, Thou shalt not slay an innocent and just man.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:54  But now, if thou sawest her, say thou, under what tree thou sawest them speaking together to themselves (or with each other)? Which said, Under an haw(thorn) tree. [Now for-sooth, if thou sawest her, say thou, under what tree thou saw them speaking to themselves (or to each other)? Which said, Under a sloe (or a blackthorn) tree.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:55  Forsooth Daniel said, Rightly thou liest in (or against) thine (own) head; for lo! the angel of the Lord, by a sentence taken of (or from) him, shall cut thee by (or across) the middle.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:56  And when he was (re)moved away, he commanded the tother to come, and said to him, Thou seed of Canaan, and not of Judah, fairness hath deceived thee, and covetousness hath mis-turned thine heart; [And him removed away, he commanded the tother for to come, and said to him, Seed of Canaan, and not of Judah, form, or fairness, deceived thee, and covetousness turned thine heart upside-down;]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:57  thus ye did to (or with) the daughters of Israel, and they dreaded, and spake to (or with) you, but the daughter of Judah suffered not (or would not allow) your wickedness.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:58  Now therefore say to me, under what tree thou sawest them speaking together to themselves (or with each other)? Which said, Under a black-thorn (tree)[or Which saith, Under a plum tree].
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:59  Forsooth Daniel said to him, Rightly also thou liest in (or against) thine (own) head; for the angel of the Lord dwelleth, and hath a sword, that he cut thee by (or across) the middle, and slay you.
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:60  Therefore all the people cried (out) loud with (a) great voice, and blessed God, that saveth them that hope in him. [And so all the people cried with great voice, and blessed the Lord, that saveth men hoping in him.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:61  And they rised (up) together against the two priests (or the two old men); for Daniel had convicted them by (or with) their (own) mouth(s), (so) that they had borne false witnessing; [And they rose together against the two priests; soothly Daniel had convicted them of their mouth, for to have said false witnessing;]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:62  and they did to them, as they had done evil (or had intended evilly to do) against the neighbouress, that they should do by the law of Moses, and they killed them. And (so the) guilt-less blood was saved in (or on) that day. [and they did to them, as they had done evil against the neighbour, that they did after the law of Moses, and slew them. And the guiltless blood is saved in that day.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:63  Forsooth Hilkiah and his wife praised the Lord in (or on) that day for Susanna, their daughter, with Joakim, her husband, and with all her kins-men, for a foul thing was not found in her. [Forsooth Hilkiah and his wife praised God in that day, for their daughter Susanna, with Joakim, her husband, and all her cousins, for foul thing was not found in her.]
DANIEL AND SUSANNA 1:64  Forsooth Daniel was made great in the sight of the people, from that day and afterward.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:1  And king Astyages was put to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia took [or received] his realm.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:2  Forsooth Daniel ate with the king, and was honoured above all the friends of him.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:3  Also an idol, Bel by name, was at Babylon, and twelve measures of clean flour, of which measures each contained three bushels, and forty sheep, and six measures of wine, that be called amphoras, were spended in it (or were spent upon it) each day.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:4  And the king worshipped that Bel, and went each day to honour him; certainly Daniel worshipped his God. And the king said to him, Why worshippest thou not Bel?
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:5  Which answered, and said to him, For I worship not idols made by hand, but God living [or (the) living God], that made (out) of nought heaven and earth, and hath power of (or over) each flesh.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:6  And the king said to him, Whether it seemeth not to thee, that Bel is a living god? whether thou seest not, how great things he eateth and drinketh each day?
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:7  And Daniel said laughing, King, err thou not; for why this Bel is (made) of clay within, and of brass withoutforth, and eateth not, [neither drinketh], any time.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:8  And the king was wroth, and called the priests thereof [or the priests of him], and said to them, If ye say not to me, who it is that eateth these costs, either expenses, ye shall die.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:9  Forsooth if ye show that Bel eateth these things, Daniel shall die, for he blasphemed Bel. And Daniel said to the king, Be it done by [or after] thy word.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:10  Forsooth the priests of Bel were seventy, besides (their) wives, and little children, either servants, and sons. And the king came with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:11  And the priests of Bel said, Lo! We shall go out, and thou, king, set (forth the) meats, and meddle (or mix the) wine, and close thou the door, and aseal it with thy ring.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:12  And when thou comest [in] early, if thou findest not all things eaten of (or by) Bel, we shall die by death, either [or] Daniel shall die, that lied against us.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:13  Soothly they trusted, for they had made a privy [or an hid] entering under the board (or they had made a secret entrance under the table), and by it they entered ever[more](or repeatedly), and devoured those things.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:14  Forsooth it was done, after that they went out, and the king setted (forth the) meats before Bel, Daniel commanded to his children (or his servants), and they brought ashes, and he riddled (them) through(out) all the temple, before the king (alone). And (then) they went out, and closed the door, and asealed (it) with the ring of the king, and went forth [or away].
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:15  But the priests entered in the night, by their custom, and the wives, and (the) children of them, and ate and drank all things.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:16  Forsooth the king rose most early, and Daniel with him.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:17  And the king said, Daniel, whether the seals be safe? And he answered, King, those (or they) be safe.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:18  And anon when they had opened the door, the king beheld the board (or at the table), and he cried on high with a great (or a loud) voice, Bel, thou art great, and no guile is at (or with) thee.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:19  And Daniel laughed, and he held the king, (so) that he entered not with-in. And Daniel said, Lo! the pavement, perceive thou whose steps these be.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:20  And the king said, I see (the) steps of men, and of women, and of young children. And the king was wroth.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:21  Then the king took (hold of) the priests, and the wives, and (the) children of them; and they showed to him (the) little privy (or secret) doors, by which they entered, and wasted those things that were on the board (or consumed those things that were on the table).
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:22  Therefore the king killed them, and betook Bel into the power of Daniel, which destroyed that Bel, and his temple.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:23  And a great dragon (or a large snake) was (also) in that place, and (the) Babylonians worshipped it.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:24  And the king said to Daniel, Lo! now thou mayest not say, that this is not a quick [or a living] god; therefore worship thou him.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:25  And Daniel said to the king, I worship my Lord God, for he is God living [or (the) living God].
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:26  But thou, king, give power to me, and I shall slay the dragon (or I will kill the snake), without sword or staff. And the king said, I give (leave) to thee.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:27  Therefore Daniel took pitch, and tallow [or fatness], and hairs, and seethed (or boiled them) together; and he made gobbets (or lumps), and gave (them) into the mouth of the dragon (or and put it into the mouth of the snake), and the dragon was all-broken [or burst]. And Daniel said, Lo! whom ye worship.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:28  And when (the) Babylonians had heard this thing, they had indignation greatly; and they were gathered (together) against the king, and said, The king is made a Jew; he destroyed Bel, and killed the dragon (or the snake), and slew [or killed] the priests.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:29  And they said, when they were come to the king, Betake thou [or Give] to us Daniel, that destroyed Bel, and killed [or slew] the dragon (or the snake); (or) else we shall slay thee, and thine house.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:30  Therefore the king saw, that they fell in on him greatly; and he was compelled by need, and he betook [or gave] Daniel to them.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:31  Which sent him into the pit of lions [or into the lake of lions], and he was there (for) seven days.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:32  Certainly seven lions were in the pit, and two bodies and two sheep were given to them each day. And then those were not given to them, (so) that they should devour Daniel.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:33  Forsooth Habakkuk, the prophet, was in Judea [or Habakkuk was a prophet in Judea], and he had sodden pottage, and had set in (or put some) loaves in a little pannier [or vessel], (or basket or bowl); and he went into the field, to bear (it) to (the) reapers.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:34  And the angel of the Lord said to Habakkuk, Bear thou the meat (or Take the meal), which thou hast, into Babylon, to Daniel, which is in the pit of (the) lions.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:35  And Habakkuk said, Lord, I saw not Babylon, and I knew not [or know not](where) the pit (is).
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:36  And the angel of the Lord took him by his top, and bare him by the hair of his head; and set him (down)[or put him (down)] in Babylon, on (or above) the pit, in the fierceness of his spirit.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:37  And Habakkuk cried, and said, Daniel, the servant of God, take thou the meat (or the meal), that God hath sent to thee.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:38  And Daniel said, Lord God, thou hast mind on me, and hast not forsaken them that love thee.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:39  And Daniel rose, and ate; certainly the angel of the Lord restored Habak-kuk anon in(to) his (own) place (again).
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:40  Therefore the king came in (or on) the seventh day to bewail Daniel; and he came to the pit, and looked in, and lo! Daniel (was) sitting in the midst of (the) lions.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:41  (And) The king cried on high with (a) great (or a loud) voice, and said, Lord God of Daniel, thou art great;
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:42  and the king drew him out of the pit. Certainly he sent into the pit them, that were (the) cause of his perdition, and they were devoured in a moment before him.
DANIEL, BEL, AND THE SNAKE 1:43  Then the king said, They that dwell in all the earth, dread the God of Daniel, for he is God living into worlds (or the living God forevermore); he is (the) deliverer, and (the) Saviour, doing miracles and marvels in heaven and in (or on the) earth, that delivered Daniel from the pit of (the) lions.
1ST MACCABEES 1:1  And it was done, after that Alexan-der (the son) of Philip, king of Mace-donia, which reigned first in Greece, and went out of the land of Kittim, smote Darius, king of Persians and of Medes or king of Persia and of Media,
1ST MACCABEES 1:2  he ordained many battles, and got strengths (or strongholds) of (or from) all; and he slew the kings of (the) earth,
1ST MACCABEES 1:3  and passed forth till to the ends of (the) earth, and took spoils of (or from a) multitude of folks; and (then) the earth was still in the sight of him.
1ST MACCABEES 1:4  And he gathered virtue, and host full strong (or And he gathered a very strong army), and the heart of him was enhanced and lift(ed) up. And he got the countries of folks, and tyrants, either strong men; and they were made to him into tribute.
1ST MACCABEES 1:5  And after these things he fell into the bed, and knew that he should die.
1ST MACCABEES 1:6  And he called his noble children (or his honourable servants), that were nourished with him from their youth, and parted to them his kingdom, when he lived yet.
1ST MACCABEES 1:7  And (so) Alexander reigned twelve years, and was dead.
1ST MACCABEES 1:8  And his children wielded the realm (or And his servants ruled the kingdom), each in his place,
1ST MACCABEES 1:9  and all putted to them diadems (or they all put crowns upon themselves) after his death, and the sons of them after them, (for) many years; and evils were multiplied in (or on the) earth.
1ST MACCABEES 1:10  And there went out of them a root of sin, Antiochus the noble (or Antiochus Epiphanes), the son of Antiochus the king, that was at Rome in hostage, and reigned in the hundred and seven and thirtieth year of the realm of (the) Greeks.
1ST MACCABEES 1:11  In those days wicked sons of Israel went out, and counselled many, and said, Go we, and ordain we [a] testa-ment (or covenant) with (the) heathen men, that be about us; for since we parted from them, many evils found us.
1ST MACCABEES 1:12  And the word was seen good before the eyes of them.
1ST MACCABEES 1:13  And some of the people sent, and went to the king; and he gave power to them for to do (the) rightfulness of (the) heathen men.
1ST MACCABEES 1:14  And they builded a school in Jerusalem, by [or after](the) laws of (the) nations;
1ST MACCABEES 1:15  and made to them prepuces (or made themselves uncircumcised), and went away from the holy testament, and were joined to (the) nations, and were sold for to do evil.
1ST MACCABEES 1:16  And the realm had prosperity in the sight of Antiochus, and he began to reign in the land of Egypt, (so) that he should reign on two realms.
1ST MACCABEES 1:17  And he entered into Egypt with a grievous multitude, in (or with) chariots, and elephants, and horsemen, either knights, and [a] plenteous multitude of ships,
1ST MACCABEES 1:18  and he ordained battle against Ptolemy, king of Egypt, and Ptolemy dreaded of his face, and flew (or fled); and many were wounded, and fell down.
1ST MACCABEES 1:19  And he took the strong cities in the land of Egypt, and [he] took the preys of the land of Egypt.
1ST MACCABEES 1:20  And Antiochus (re)turned, after that he (had) smote Egypt, in the hundred and three and fortieth year, and went up to Israel. And he went up to Jerusalem with a grievous multitude,
1ST MACCABEES 1:21  and entered into the hallowing (or the Temple) with pride; and he took (away) the golden altar, and the candle-stick of light, and all the vessels thereof,
1ST MACCABEES 1:22  and the board of proposition (or the table of the showbread), and (the) vessels of floating (or liquid) sacrifices, and cruets, and golden mortars, and veil, and crowns, and golden ornament that was in the face (or on the front) of the temple; and he brake all.
1ST MACCABEES 1:23  And he took (the) silver and (the) gold, and all (the) desirable vessels, and he took the privy (or hidden) treasures, which he found;
1ST MACCABEES 1:24  and when he had taken up all things, he went into his land. And he made (a) slaughter of men, and spake in (or with) great pride.
1ST MACCABEES 1:25  And great wailing was made in Israel, and in each place of them;
1ST MACCABEES 1:26  and (the) princes sorrowed inward-ly, and elder men, and (the) maidens, and (the) young men were made sick (or feeble), and (the) fairness of women was changed.
1ST MACCABEES 1:27  Each husband took (up) wailing, and they that sat in (the) husband’s bed, mourned.
1ST MACCABEES 1:28  And the land was moved (al)to-gether on (or for the) men dwelling therein, and all the house of Jacob was clothed with confusion.
1ST MACCABEES 1:29  And after two years of days, the king sent a prince of tributes into the cities of Judea, and he came to Jerusalem with (a) great company.
1ST MACCABEES 1:30  And he spake to them peaceable words in guile, and they believed to him. And suddenly he fell in on the city, and smote it with a great wound, and lost much people of Israel.
